title: حِكَايَةُ الصَّبِيَّةِ الثَّانِيَةِ: الْعَجُوزُ وَالشَّابُّ الْغَادِرُ
titleEn: The Second Lady's Tale: The Old Woman, the Wedding, and the Beating
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 128–139 (Night 18, continuing directly from nights-17), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 18 closes the youngest sister's tale (the serpent-jinn, the two sisters turned into black dogs, and the daily beating) and gives the tale of the second lady, whose scarred body the caliph asks about. A wealthy widow, she is lured by an old woman to a splendid house and married to a handsome youth on his oath that she look at no other man; a shopkeeper's price for cloth is a kiss, he bites her cheek, and her husband, discovering the wound, has her beaten by slaves and left half-dead. Verse abounds and is copied as printed. The night ends when the caliph, having heard all three ladies, has the story recorded, and dawn cuts Shahrazad off. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularized the language here and there, so some of the original Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّامِنَةَ عَشَرَ قَٰلَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thāminata ʿashara qālat
sentences.l: So when it was the eighteenth night, she said:
sentences.n: The edition prints قل, which would be قُلْتُ 'I said'. Because this is the regular night formula, and Shahrazad is the one speaking, it is read as the defective spelling of قَالَتْ 'she said' (the dagger alif marks the missing alif).

sentences.t: بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الصَّبِيَّةَ مَا زَالَتْ تُحَسِّنُ لِلشَّابِّ التَّوَجُّهَ مَعَنَا حَتَّى قَالَ لِي نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-ṣabiyyata mā zālat tuḥassinu li-al-shābbi al-tawajjuha maʿanā ḥattā qāla lī naʿam
sentences.l: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the girl did not cease making-fair to the youth the going-off with us, until he said to me: Yes.
sentences.i: It has reached me, O fortunate King, that the girl never ceased to urge the youth to come away with us, until at last he said to me, "Yes."
sentences.n: مَا زَالَ plus a verb means 'kept on doing', literally 'did not cease'. The girl speaking in the tale is the one telling it to the caliph; Shahrazad here narrates her words in the third person for a moment.

sentences.t: فَبِتُّ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ تَحْتَ رِجْلَيْهِ وَأَنَا لَا أُصَدِّقُ مَا أَنَا فِيهِ مِنَ الْفَرَحِ
sentences.tr: fa-bittu tilka al-laylata taḥta rijlayhi wa-anā lā uṣaddiqu mā anā fīhi mina al-faraḥi
sentences.l: So I spent-the-night that night beneath his two feet, and I was not believing what I was in, of the joy.
sentences.i: So I passed that night at his feet, hardly able to believe the joy that I was in.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ قُمْنَا وَدَخَلْنَا إِلَى الْخَزَائِنِ وَأَخَذْنَا مَا خَفَّ حَمْلُهُ وَغَلَا ثَمَنُهُ وَنَزَلْنَا مِنَ الْقَلْعَةِ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ فَقَابَلَنَا الْعَبِيدُ وَالرَّئِيسُ وَ هُمْ يُفَتِّشُونَ عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu qumnā wa-dakhalnā ilā al-khazāʾini wa-akhadhnā mā khaffa ḥamluhu wa-ghalā thamanuhu wa-nazalnā mina al-qalʿati ilā al-madīnati fa-qābalanā al-ʿabīdu wa-al-raʾīsu wa hum yufattishūna ʿalayya
sentences.l: So when the morning became morning, we rose and entered to the treasuries, and took what was light its carrying and dear its price, and we went down from the citadel to the city; and the slaves met us, and the captain, and they were searching for me.
sentences.i: When morning came, we rose and went into the treasuries, and took whatever was light to carry and dear in price. Then we went down from the citadel to the city, and there the slaves met us, with the captain, who were searching for me.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْنِي فَرِحُوا وَأَخْبَرْتُهُمْ بِمَا رَأَيْتُ وَحَكَيْتُ لَهُمْ عَلَى قِصَّةِ الشَّابِّ وَسَبَبِ سَخَطِ هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَمَا جَرَا لَهُمْ فَتَعَجَّبُوا مِنْ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾawnī fariḥū wa-akhbartuhum bi-mā raʾaytu wa-ḥakaytu lahum ʿalā qiṣṣati al-shābbi wa-sababi sakhaṭi hādhihi al-madīnati wa-mā jarā lahum fa-taʿajjabū min dhālika
sentences.l: So when they saw me they rejoiced, and I informed them of what I had seen, and I related to them upon the story of the youth, and the cause of the wrath of this city, and what had run to them; and they marvelled at that.
sentences.i: When they saw me they rejoiced, and I told them what I had seen, and related to them the story of the youth, the reason for the wrath that fell on this city, and what had befallen its people; and they marvelled at it.
sentences.n: حَكَيْتُ لَهُمْ عَلَى قِصَّةِ is a loose construction: the verb 'relate' takes its object directly in Classical Arabic, and here عَلَى is simply added. جَرَا is the edition's spelling of جَرَى (alif for final yāʾ); the same spelling recurs below.

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا رَأَوْنِي أَخَوَاتِي هَاتَيْنِ الْكَلْبَتَيْنِ وَمَعِي ذَلِكَ الشَّابُّ حَسَدُونِي عَلَيْهِ وَصَارُوا فِي غَيْظٍ وَأَضْمَرُوا الْمَكْرَ ثُمَّ طَلَعْنَا الْمَرْكَبَ فَرِحِينَ وَنَحْنُ طَائِرِينَ مِنَ الْفَرَحِ بِالْكَسْبِ
sentences.tr: wa-lammā raʾawnī akhawātī hātayni al-kalbatayni wa-maʿī dhālika al-shābbu ḥasadūnī ʿalayhi wa-ṣārū fī ghayẓin wa-aḍmarū al-makra thumma ṭalaʿnā al-markaba fariḥīna wa-naḥnu ṭāʾirīna mina al-faraḥi bi-al-kasbi
sentences.l: And when they saw me, my sisters, these two bitches, and with me that youth, they envied me over him, and became in rage, and hid-inwardly the plot; then we went-up the ship rejoicing, and we were flying from the joy at the gain.
sentences.i: When my sisters, these two bitches, saw me with that youth beside me, they envied me for him and seethed with rage, and they hid a plot in their hearts. Then we boarded the ship, rejoicing, and we were fairly flying with joy at our gain.
sentences.n: The verbs رَأَوْنِي and حَسَدُونِي are masculine plural, though the subject is two women; the subject is also placed after the verb as an apposition, and هَاتَيْنِ الْكَلْبَتَيْنِ 'these two bitches' is the narrator's later label for them, read back into the story. These are Middle Arabic looseness, kept as printed. بِالْكَسْبِ here means 'because of, at' the gain.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا فَرَحِي أَكْثَرُ كَانَ بِالشَّابِّ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā faraḥī aktharu kāna bi-al-shābbi
sentences.l: But as for my joy, most was in the youth.
sentences.i: But my greatest joy was in the youth.
sentences.n: أَكْثَرُ كَانَ is not Classical (one would expect أَكْثَرُ فَرَحِي كَانَ or كَانَ فَرَحِي أَكْثَرَ); it is read as 'the greater part of my joy was in the youth', and بِـ means 'in, on account of'.

sentences.t: وَأَقَمْنَا نَنْتَظِرُ الرِّيحَ فَطَابَ لَنَا الرِّيحُ فَرَفَعْنَا الْقُلُوعَ وَسَافَرْنَا فَقَعَدَتْ أَخَوَانِي عِنْدَنَا وَصِرْنَا نَتَحَدَّثُ
sentences.tr: wa-aqamnā nantaẓiru al-rīḥa fa-ṭāba lanā al-rīḥu fa-rafaʿnā al-qulūʿa wa-sāfarnā fa-qaʿadat akhawānī ʿindanā wa-ṣirnā nataḥaddathu
sentences.l: And we stayed, waiting for the wind, and the wind became-good for us, so we raised the sails and set out; and my brothers sat with us, and we began conversing.
sentences.i: We stayed waiting for a wind, and the wind turned fair for us; so we hoisted the sails and put to sea. My sisters sat down beside us, and we fell to talking.
sentences.n: The edition prints اخواني, which would be 'my two brothers'; the feminine verb قَعَدَتْ and the following فَقَالَتَا show that the two sisters are meant, so this is a slip for أَخَوَاتِي. It is vocalised as printed. طَابَ لَنَا الرِّيحُ 'the wind became pleasant to us' is the ordinary sailor's phrase for a fair wind; الرِّيح is treated as masculine here.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتَا لِي يَا أُخْتَنَا مَا تَصْنَعِينَ مَعَ هَذَا الشَّابِّ الْحَسَنِ فَقُلْتُ لَهُمْ قَصْدِي أَتَّخِذُهُ بَعْلًا
sentences.tr: fa-qālatā lī yā ukhtanā mā taṣnaʿīna maʿa hādhā al-shābbi al-ḥasani fa-qultu lahum qaṣdī attakhidhuhu baʿlan
sentences.l: So the two said to me: O our sister, what will you do with this handsome youth? So I said to them: My intention is I take him as a husband.
sentences.i: The two of them said to me, "Sister, what will you do with this handsome youth?" And I said, "My aim is to take him for my husband."
sentences.n: قَصْدِي أَتَّخِذُهُ 'my intention: I take him' puts a bare verb after a noun with no أَنْ; this is normal in Middle Arabic. لَهُمْ is masculine plural for two women, as printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ الْتَفَتُّ إِلَيْهِ وَأَقْبَلْتُ عَلَيْهِ وَقُلْتُ يَا سَيِّدِي قَصْدِي أَقُولُ لَكَ شَيْئًا لَاتُخَالِفْنِي فِيهِ
sentences.tr: thumma iltafattu ilayhi wa-aqbaltu ʿalayhi wa-qultu yā sayyidī qaṣdī aqūlu laka shayʾan lā tukhālifnī fīhi
sentences.l: Then I turned to him and approached upon him and said: O my master, my intention is I say to you a thing; do not oppose me in it.
sentences.i: Then I turned to him and faced him, and said, "My lord, I wish to tell you something. Do not cross me in it."
sentences.n: لَاتُخَالِفْنِي is printed as one word, لَا + تُخَالِفْنِي.

sentences.t: وَهُوَ أَنَّهُ إِذَا وَصَلْنَا إِلَى بَغْدَادَ مَدِينَتِنَا فَأَنَا أُقَدِّمُ نَفْسِي لَكَ جَارِيَةً بِرَسْمِ الْحَرَمِ وَتَكُونُ لِي بَعْلًا وَأَكُونُ أَنَا لَكَ أَهْلًا
sentences.tr: wa-huwa annahu idhā waṣalnā ilā Baghdāda madīnatinā fa-anā uqaddimu nafsī laka jāriyatan bi-rasmi al-ḥarami wa-takūnu lī baʿlan wa-akūnu anā laka ahlan
sentences.l: And it is that, when we arrive at Baghdad, our city, then I present my self to you as a slave-girl, for the purpose of the harem, and you will be for me a husband, and I will be, I, for you a wife.
sentences.i: It is this: when we reach Baghdad, our city, I shall offer myself to you as a slave-girl for your harem; you shall be my husband, and I shall be your wife.
sentences.n: بِرَسْمِ الْحَرَمِ 'by way of, for the purpose of the harem': رَسْم here is 'designation, purpose', and بِـ marks the purpose. جَارِيَةً is accusative as a state ('as a slave-girl'). أَهْل is literally 'family, kin', and in the sense 'wife' is regular.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ سَمْعًا وَ طَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla samʿan wa ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: So he said: Hearing and obedience.
sentences.i: He answered with hearing and obedience.
sentences.n: The edition prints a stray و apart from طَاعَةً (a line break separates them). سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً is an accusative pair of verbal nouns ('I give hearing and obedience'), the standard formula of assent.

sentences.t: وَالْتَفَتُّ إِلَى أَخَوَاتِي وَقُلْتُ لَهُمْ يَكْفِينِي هَذَا الشَّابُّ وَكُلُّ مَنْ كَسَبَ شَيْئًا فَهُوَ لَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-iltafattu ilā akhawātī wa-qultu lahum yakfīnī hādhā al-shābbu wa-kullu man kasaba shayʾan fa-huwa lahu
sentences.l: And I turned to my sisters and said to them: This youth suffices me; and everyone who has gained a thing, it is his.
sentences.i: Then I turned to my sisters and said, "This youth is enough for me; and whatever each of us has gained is her own."
sentences.n: كُلُّ مَنْ كَسَبَ شَيْئًا فَهُوَ لَهُ is a general rule ('whoever gains something, it is his'); the masculine is generic, and here means that each sister keeps her own gain.

sentences.t: فَقُلْنَ لِي نِعْمَ مَا فَعَلْتِ
sentences.tr: fa-qulna lī niʿma mā faʿalti
sentences.l: So they said to me: Excellent what you have done.
sentences.i: They said to me, "You have done well."

sentences.t: لَكِنَّهُمْ أَضْمَرُوا لِي الشَّرَّ وَلَمْ نَزَلْ سَائِرِينَ
sentences.tr: lākinnahum aḍmarū lī al-sharra wa-lam nazal sāʾirīna
sentences.l: But they hid-inwardly for me the evil, and we did not cease going-on.
sentences.i: But they hid evil against me in their hearts, and we sailed on without pause.
sentences.n: The edition prints ولم and نزل on separate lines; they are one phrase, وَلَمْ نَزَلْ 'and we did not cease'. Again لَكِنَّهُمْ is masculine for the two sisters. أَضْمَرَ لَهُ الشَّرَّ 'to harbour evil for him' takes لِـ of the person harmed.

sentences.t: وَطَابَ لَنَا الرِّيحُ حَتَّى خَرَجْنَا مِنْ بَحْرِ الْخَوْفِ وَدَخَلْنَا الْأَمَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-ṭāba lanā al-rīḥu ḥattā kharajnā min baḥri al-khawfi wa-dakhalnā al-amāna
sentences.l: And the wind was good to us until we came out from the sea of fear and entered safety.
sentences.i: The wind stayed fair to us until we came out of the sea of fear and entered into safety.

sentences.t: وَسَافَرْنَا أَيَّامًا قَلَائِلَ إِلَى أَنْ قَرُبْنَا مِنْ مَدِينَةِ الْبَصْرَةِ وَلَاحَتْ لَنَا أَسْوَارُهَا فَأَدْرَكَنَا الْمَسَاءُ
sentences.tr: wa-sāfarnā ayyāman qalāʾila ilā an qarubnā min madīnati al-Baṣrati wa-lāḥat lanā aswāruhā fa-adrakanā al-masāʾu
sentences.l: And we travelled some few days until we drew near from the city of Basra, and its walls shone-out to us, and the evening overtook us.
sentences.i: We voyaged a few days more, until we drew near the city of Basra and its walls came into view; and evening overtook us.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَخَذَنَا النَّوْمُ قَامَتْ أَخَوَاتِي وَحَمَلُونِي بِفِرَاشِي وَرَمَتْنِي فِي الْبَحْرِ وَكَذَلِكَ فَعَلُوا بِالشَّابِّ وَكَانَ لَا يُحْسِنُ الْعَوْمَ فَغَرِقَ وَكَتَبَهُ اللَّهُ مِنَ الشُّهَدَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā akhadhanā al-nawmu qāmat akhawātī wa-ḥamalūnī bi-firāshī wa-ramatnī fī al-baḥri wa-ka-dhālika faʿalū bi-al-shābbi wa-kāna lā yuḥsinu al-ʿawma fa-ghariqa wa-katabahu Allāhu mina al-shuhadāʾi
sentences.l: So when sleep took us, my sisters rose, and they carried me with my bedding, and she threw me into the sea; and likewise they did with the youth, and he was not skilled at swimming, so he drowned, and God wrote him among the martyrs.
sentences.i: When sleep had taken us, my sisters rose and lifted me up together with my bedding and cast me into the sea. They did the same to the youth, who could not swim; so he drowned, and God recorded him among the martyrs.
sentences.n: The verbs shift between masculine plural (وَحَمَلُونِي, فَعَلُوا) and feminine singular (قَامَتْ, وَرَمَتْنِي) for the same two sisters, as printed. كَتَبَهُ اللَّهُ مِنَ الشُّهَدَاءِ 'God wrote him (down) among the martyrs': a drowned man is counted a martyr in Islamic tradition.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا أَنَا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ غَرِقْتُ مَعَهُ وَلَكِنْ قَدَّرَ اللَّهُ أَنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ السَّالِمِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā anā laytanī kuntu ghariqtu maʿahu wa-lākin qaddara Allāhu annī kuntu mina al-sālimīna
sentences.l: But as for me, would that I had drowned with him; but God decreed that I was of the safe-ones.
sentences.i: As for me, I wish I had drowned with him; but God decreed that I should be among the saved.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا اسْتَقْرَيْتُ فِي الْبَحْرِ رَزَقَنِي اللَّهُ بِقِطْعَةِ خَشَبٍ فَرَكِبْتُهَا وَضَرَبَتْنِي الْأَمْوَاجُ إِلَى أَنْ رَمَتْنِي عَلَى سَاحِلِ جَزِيرَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā istaqraytu fī al-baḥri razaqanī Allāhu bi-qiṭʿati khashabin fa-rakibtuhā wa-ḍarabatnī al-amwāju ilā an ramatnī ʿalā sāḥili jazīratin
sentences.l: So when I found-myself-settled in the sea, God provided me with a piece of wood, and I mounted it, and the waves struck me until they threw me upon the shore of an island.
sentences.i: When I found myself in the sea, God provided me with a piece of timber. I climbed upon it, and the waves drove me on until they threw me up on the shore of an island.
sentences.n: اسْتَقْرَيْتُ is printed as it stands; it is taken as a form of اسْتَقَرَّ 'to settle, find oneself' (with the doubled letter written out as a weak one, a Middle Arabic habit). The sense 'when I found myself in the sea' seems sure. رَزَقَنِي اللَّهُ بِقِطْعَةِ خَشَبٍ 'God provided me with a piece of wood': بِـ names what was given.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ أَزَلْ أَمْشِي فِي الْجَزِيرَةِ بَاقِيَ لَيْلَتِي وَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ رَأَيْتُ طَرِيقًا مُشِىَ عَلَى قَدْرِ قَدَمِ ابْنِ آدَمَ مُتَّصِلَةً مِنَ الْجَزِيرَةِ إِلَى الْبَرِّ
sentences.tr: fa-lam azal amshī fī al-jazīrati bāqiya laylatī wa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu raʾaytu ṭarīqan mushiya ʿalā qadri qadami ibni Ādama muttaṣilatan mina al-jazīrati ilā al-barri
sentences.l: So I did not cease walking in the island the remainder of my night; and when the morning became morning I saw a path walked-on upon the measure of the foot of a son of Adam, connected from the island to the mainland.
sentences.i: I walked on through the island for the rest of my night, and when morning came I saw a path, no wider than a man's footprint, trodden through from the island to the mainland.
sentences.n: مُشِىَ 'was walked' is one possible reading of the printed مشى; the other is مَشَى 'walked' with the path as its subject, which is odd. The idea is a track worn only as broad as a human foot. ابْنِ آدَمَ 'son of Adam' means simply 'a human being'. مُتَّصِلَةً is feminine to agree with طَرِيقًا, which can be treated as feminine.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ طَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ فَنَشَّفْتُ أَثْوَابِي فِي الشَّمْسِ وَأَكَلْتُ مِنْ ثِمَارِ الْجَزِيرَةِ وَشَرِبْتُ مِنْ مَائِهَا وَسِرْتُ فِي الطَّرِيقِ وَلَمْ أَزَلْ سَائِرَةً إِلَى أَنْ قَرُبْتُ مِنَ الْبَرِّ وَقَدْ بَقِيَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ الْمَدِينَةِ سَاعَتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad ṭalaʿati al-shamsu fa-nashshaftu athwābī fī al-shamsi wa-akaltu min thimāri al-jazīrati wa-sharibtu min māʾihā wa-sirtu fī al-ṭarīqi wa-lam azal sāʾiratan ilā an qarubtu mina al-barri wa-qad baqiya baynī wa-bayna al-madīnati sāʿatayni
sentences.l: And the sun had risen, so I dried my clothes in the sun, and ate from the fruits of the island, and drank from its water, and went on the path, and did not cease going until I drew near the mainland, and there had remained between me and the city two hours.
sentences.i: The sun was up by then, so I dried my clothes in its light, ate some of the island's fruit, drank from its water, and set out along the path. I went on and on until I neared the mainland, with only two hours left between me and the city.
sentences.n: سَاعَتَيْنِ is printed in the oblique dual although it is the subject of بَقِيَ (Classical سَاعَتَانِ); it is kept as printed. The 'hours' are travelling time, i.e. about two hours' walk.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا أَنَا بِحَيَّةٍ عَامِلَةٍ عَلَيَّ وَهِيَ فِي غِلَظِ النَّخْلَةِ تَسْعَى سَعْيًا مُسْرِعًا وَقَدْ أَقْبَلَتْ نَحْوِي فَرَأَيْتُهَا تَأْخُذُ يَمِينًا وَشِمَالًا حَتَّى وَصَلَتْ عِنْدِي
sentences.tr: wa-idhā anā bi-ḥayyatin ʿāmilatin ʿalayya wa-hiya fī ghilaẓi al-nakhlati tasʿā saʿyan musriʿan wa-qad aqbalat naḥwī fa-raʾaytuhā taʾkhudhu yamīnan wa-shimālan ḥattā waṣalat ʿindī
sentences.l: And behold, I was with a serpent working upon me, and she was in the thickness of a palm-tree, running a hastening running, and she had come toward me; and I saw her taking right and left until she reached at me.
sentences.i: And behold, there was a serpent bearing down on me, as thick as a palm-trunk, running at a great speed. She had come straight toward me; I saw her swerving right and left until she came right up to me.
sentences.n: وَإِذَا أَنَا بِـ ... 'and behold, I was with...' is the formula of sudden surprise: the بِـ only marks what appears, here the serpent. عَامِلَةً عَلَيَّ, literally 'working upon me', means she was making at me, bearing down on me. In the tale this serpent is a female jinn in serpent form, so the feminine is used throughout.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا بِلِسَانِهَا قَدْ تَدَلَّى عَلَى الْأَرْضِ مِقْدَارَ شِبْرٍ وَتَجْرُفُ التُّرَابَ بِطُولِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-idhā bi-lisānihā qad tadallā ʿalā al-arḍi miqdāra shibrin wa-tajrufu al-turāba bi-ṭūlihā
sentences.l: And behold, by her tongue, which had hung down on the ground the measure of a span, and she sweeps the dust with her length.
sentences.i: And there was her tongue, hanging down to the ground a span's length, while she swept the dust along with her whole length.
sentences.n: فَإِذَا بِلِسَانِهَا: again إِذَا + بِـ of surprise, 'and behold, her tongue'; the بِـ adds nothing but the sense of a sudden sight. In the last clause بِـ means 'with', i.e. 'by means of her length'.

sentences.t: وَ خَلْفَهَا ثُعْبَانٌ طَارَدَهَا وَهُوَ طَوِيلٌ رَقِيقٌ طُولَ رُمْحٍ وَهِيَ هَارِبَةٌ مِنْهُ وَ تَلْتَفِتُ يَمِينًا وَشِمَالًا وَقَدْ قَبَضَ ذَنَبَهَا وَسَالَتْ دَمْعَهَا وَقَدْ تَدَلَّى لِسَانُهَا مِنْ شِدَّةِ الْهَرَبِ
sentences.tr: wa-khalfahā thuʿbānun ṭārada-hā wa-huwa ṭawīlun raqīqun ṭūla rumḥin wa-hiya hāribatun minhu wa-taltafitu yamīnan wa-shimālan wa-qad qabaḍa dhanabahā wa-sālat damʿahā wa-qad tadallā lisānuhā min shiddati al-harabi
sentences.l: And behind her a great-snake, chasing her, and he was long, slender, the length of a spear; and she was fleeing from him, and turning right and left; and he had seized her tail, and her tear flowed, and her tongue had hung down from the intensity of the flight.
sentences.i: Behind her came a great snake in pursuit, long and slender, as long as a spear. She was fleeing from him, glancing right and left, for he had caught hold of her tail; her tears ran down, and her tongue hung out from the violence of her flight.
sentences.n: The printed قبض ذنبها may be read either قَبَضَ ذَنَبَهَا 'he had seized her tail' (taken here) or قُبِضَ ذَنَبُهَا 'her tail was seized'; the sense is nearly the same. سَالَتْ دَمْعَهَا puts 'her tear' in the accusative after a verb that should take it as subject (سَالَ دَمْعُهَا); this is kept as printed. The ثُعْبَان is a large snake, and the tale calls it a male jinn.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَتْنِي الشَّفَقَةُ عَلَيْهَا فَعَمِلْتُ إِلَى حَجَرٍ وَأَلْقَيْتُهُ عَلَى رَأْسِ الثُّعْبَانِ فَمَاتَ مِنْ وَقْتِهِ فَفَتَحَتِ الْحَيَّةُ جَنَاحَيْنِ وَطَارَتْ فِي الْجَوِّ حَتَّى غَابَتْ مِنْ عَيْنِي
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhatnī al-shafaqatu ʿalayhā fa-ʿamiltu ilā ḥajarin wa-alqaytuhu ʿalā raʾsi al-thuʿbāni fa-māta min waqtihi fa-fataḥati al-ḥayyatu janāḥayni wa-ṭārat fī al-jawwi ḥattā ghābat min ʿaynī
sentences.l: So pity took me for her, and I worked to a stone and threw it upon the head of the great-snake, and he died from his time; and the serpent opened two wings and flew in the air until she was absent from my eye.
sentences.i: Pity for her seized me. I went for a stone and hurled it at the snake's head, and he died on the spot. Then the serpent spread two wings and flew into the air, until she was lost to my sight.
sentences.n: عَمِلْتُ إِلَى حَجَرٍ, literally 'I worked to a stone', means 'I made for a stone, I set about getting one': عَمِلَ إِلَى is a Middle Arabic use. مِنْ وَقْتِهِ 'from his time' means 'at that very moment'.

sentences.t: وَجَلَسْتُ أَتَعَجَّبُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَقَدْ تَعِبْتُ وَ لَحِقَنِي النُّعَاسُ فَنِمْتُ مَوْضِعِي سَاعَةً
sentences.tr: wa-jalastu ataʿajjabu min dhālika wa-qad taʿibtu wa laḥiqanī al-nuʿāsu fa-nimtu mawḍiʿī sāʿatan
sentences.l: And I sat marvelling at that, and I had grown tired, and drowsiness overtook me, so I slept in my place an hour.
sentences.i: I sat down, marvelling at what I had seen. I was weary, and drowsiness overtook me, so I slept where I was for an hour.
sentences.n: The edition prints a stray و before لَحِقَنِي, which begins a new clause ('and drowsiness overtook me'); it is kept as printed. مَوْضِعِي is accusative of place, 'in my place'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَفَقْتُ وَجَدْتُ تَحْتَ رِجْلَيَّ جَارِيَةً وَمَعَهَا كَلْبَتَانِ وَهِيَ تَكْبِسُ رِجْلَيَّ فَاسْتَحْيَيْتُ مِنْهَا وَقَعَدْتُ جَالِسًا وَقُلْتُ لَهَا يَا أُخْتِي مَنْ تَكُونِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā afaqtu wajadtu taḥta rijlayya jāriyatan wa-maʿahā kalbatāni wa-hiya takbisu rijlayya fa-istaḥyaytu minhā wa-qaʿadtu jālisan wa-qultu lahā yā ukhtī man takūnī
sentences.l: So when I awoke I found beneath my two feet a girl, and with her two bitches, and she was kneading my two feet; so I felt shy before her, and sat sitting, and said to her: O my sister, who are you?
sentences.i: When I woke, I found a young woman at my feet, with two bitches beside her, and she was kneading my feet. I was ashamed before her, and sat upright, and said to her, "Sister, who are you?"
sentences.n: The edition prints رجلي, which may be the dual 'my two feet' (as read here) or the singular 'my foot'; the dual is more natural for massaging. جَالِسًا is masculine although the speaker is a woman, and مَنْ تَكُونِي (for مَنْ تَكُونِينَ) drops the final nūn; both are Middle Arabic and kept as printed. اسْتَحْيَا مِنْهَا 'to be shy before her': مِنْ names the person one is ashamed in front of.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ مَا أَسْرَعَ مَا نَسِيتِنِي
sentences.tr: fa-qālat mā asraʿa mā nasītinī
sentences.l: So she said: How quick that you have forgotten me!
sentences.i: She said, "How quickly you have forgotten me!"
sentences.n: مَا أَسْرَعَ مَا نَسِيتِنِي 'how quick (it is) that you forgot me': the first مَا is the exclamatory 'how!', and the second is the verbal-noun particle.

sentences.t: أَنَا الَّتِي عَمِلْتِ مَعِي الْجَمِيلَ وَزَرَعْتِ الْمَعْرُوفَ وَقَتَلْتِ عَلْوِي فَأَنَا الْحَيَّةُ الَّتِي خَلَّصْتِنِي مِنَ الثُّعْبَانِ
sentences.tr: anā allatī ʿamilti maʿī al-jamīla wa-zaraʿti al-maʿrūfa wa-qataltī ʿAlwī fa-anā al-ḥayyatu allatī khallaṣtinī mina al-thuʿbāni
sentences.l: I am she who did with me the kindness, and sowed the good, and killed ʿAlwī; so I am the serpent who delivered me from the great-snake.
sentences.i: "I am the one to whom you did that kindness, and sowed that good deed, and killed ʿAlwī. I am the serpent you saved from the snake.
sentences.n: The verbs after اَلَّتِي are second person feminine (عَمِلْتِ, زَرَعْتِ, قَتَلْتِ, خَلَّصْتِنِي), addressed to the listener, while اَلَّتِي is third person; the agreement follows the sense, 'I am the one for whom you did...'. عَمِلَ مَعَهُ الْجَمِيلَ 'to do a kindness with him'. عَلْوِي is a personal name of the snake-jinn (perhaps ʿAlwī); the vocalisation is a guess. زَرَعَ الْمَعْرُوفَ 'sowed the good' is the image of a kindness that will bear fruit.

sentences.t: فَإِنِّي جِنِّيَّةٌ وَهَذَا الثُّعْبَانُ جِنِّيٌّ وَهُوَ عَلْوِي وَمَا نَجَاتِي مِنْهُ إِلَّا بِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-innī jinniyyatun wa-hādhā al-thuʿbānu jinniyyun wa-huwa ʿAlwī wa-mā najātī minhu illā bi-ki
sentences.l: For I am a female jinni, and this great-snake is a jinni, and he is ʿAlwī, and my deliverance from him is not except through you.
sentences.i: I am a she-jinni, and this snake was a jinni, that ʿAlwī; and I could not have escaped him but for you.
sentences.n: إِلَّا بِكِ 'except by you': the بِـ marks the means, 'through you'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَجَّيْتِنِي مِنْهُ طِرْتُ فِي الرِّيحِ وَرُحْتُ إِلَى الْمَرْكَبِ الَّتِي رَمَوْكِ مِنْهَا أَخَوَاتُكِ فَنَقَلْتُ جَمِيعَ مَا فِيهَا إِلَى بَيْتِكِ وَغَرَّقْتُهَا وَأَمَّا أَخَوَاتُكِ فَجَعَلْتُهُمَا كَلْبَتَيْنِ سُودًا فَإِنِّي عَرَفْتُ جَمِيعَ مَا جَرَى لَكِ مَعَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā najjaytinī minhu ṭirtu fī al-rīḥi wa-ruḥtu ilā al-markabi allatī ramawki minhā akhawātuki fa-naqaltu jamīʿa mā fīhā ilā baytiki wa-gharraqtuhā wa-ammā akhawātuki fa-jaʿaltuhumā kalbatayni sūdan fa-innī ʿaraftu jamīʿa mā jarā laki maʿahum
sentences.l: So when you saved me from him, I flew in the wind, and went to the ship, the one they threw you from, your sisters; and I moved all that was in it to your house, and sank it; and as for your sisters, I made them two bitches, black; for I knew all that had run to you with them.
sentences.i: When you had saved me from him, I flew off on the wind and went to the ship from which your sisters had thrown you. I carried everything in it to your house, and sank the ship. As for your sisters, I turned them into two black bitches, for I knew all that they had done to you.
sentences.n: رَمَوْكِ مِنْهَا أَخَوَاتُكِ has a masculine plural verb followed by its subject, the same looseness as above. الْمَرْكَب is treated as feminine (الَّتِي), as ships usually are. سُودًا 'black' (plural) stands beside a dual object; in the earlier sentence of this night the edition prints السُّودِ. جَعَلْتُهُمَا كَلْبَتَيْنِ 'I made them into two bitches': جَعَلَ takes two objects. مَعَهُمْ 'with them' means 'at their hands', and they are again masculine plural.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا الشَّابُّ فَإِنَّهُ غَرِقَ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā al-shābbu fa-innahu ghariqa
sentences.l: And as for the youth, he drowned.
sentences.i: As for the youth, he was drowned.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَمَلَتْنِي وَ الْكَلْبَتَيْنِ وَرَمَتْنَا فَوْقَ سَطْحِ دَارِي فَرَأَيْتُ جَمِيعَ مَا كَانَ فِى الْمَرْكَبِ مِنَ الْأَمْوَالِ فِي وَسَطِ بَيْتِي وَلَمْ يَضِعْ مِنْهُ شَيْءٌ
sentences.tr: thumma ḥamalatnī wa al-kalbatayni wa-ramatnā fawqa saṭḥi dārī fa-raʾaytu jamīʿa mā kāna fī al-markabi mina al-amwāli fī wasaṭi baytī wa-lam yaḍiʿ minhu shayʾun
sentences.l: Then she carried me and the two bitches, and threw us on top of the roof of my house; and I saw all that was in the ship, of the wealth, in the middle of my house, and nothing was lost of it.
sentences.i: Then she picked me up, with the two bitches, and flung us onto the roof of my house. There I saw all the wealth that had been in the ship, in the middle of my house, and not a thing of it was lost.
sentences.n: The edition prints a stray و (apart from الْكَلْبَتَيْنِ) after حَمَلَتْنِي; it is the ordinary 'and' in 'me and the two bitches'. The 'I' now speaking is the first sister, the narrator of the tale. مِنَ الْأَمْوَالِ 'of the wealth' explains مَا 'all that was'.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْحَيَّةَ قَالَتْ لِي وَ حَقِّ النَّقْشِ الَّذِي عَلَى خَاتَمِ سَيِّدِنَا سُلَيْمَانَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ إِذَا لَمْ تَضْرِبِي كُلَّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ ثَلَٰثَمِائَةَ سَوْطٍ جِئْتُ وَجَعَلْتُكِ مِثْلَهُمَا
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-ḥayyata qālat lī wa-ḥaqqi al-naqshi alladhī ʿalā khātami sayyidinā Sulaymāna ʿalayhi al-salāmu idhā lam taḍribī kulla wāḥidatin minhunna kulla yawmin thalāthamiʾata sawṭin jiʾtu wa-jaʿaltuki mithlahumā
sentences.l: Then the serpent said to me: And by the right of the engraving which is upon the seal of our master Solomon, upon him peace: if you do not beat each one of them each day three hundred lashes, I will come and make you like the two of them.
sentences.i: Then the serpent said to me, "By the truth of the engraving on the seal of our lord Solomon, peace be upon him: if you do not beat each of them three hundred lashes every day, I shall come and turn you into the likeness of those two."
sentences.n: وَ حَقِّ النَّقْشِ: the edition prints the و apart from its host (a line break); it is the و of oath, 'by the right of...', and the genitive حَقِّ follows from it. The engraving is the Greatest Name of God said to be cut in Solomon's seal, by which he ruled the jinn. ثَلَٰثَمِائَةَ is printed ثلثمائة without an alif after the second ل; the dagger alif supplies it. تَضْرِبِي addresses a woman in the subjunctive, and the printed spelling omits the nūn as Classical grammar requires after إِذَا لَمْ.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qultu samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: So I said: Hearing and obedience.
sentences.i: I answered with hearing and obedience.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ أَزَلْ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَضْرِبُهُمَا ذَلِكَ الضَّرْبَ وَأُشْفِقُ عَلَيْهِمَا وَهُمَا يَعْرِفَانِ أَنَّ مَا لِي ذَنْبٌ فِي ضَرْبِهِمَا وَيَقْبَلَانِ عُذْرِي
sentences.tr: fa-lam azal yā amīra al-muʾminīna aḍribuhumā dhālika al-ḍarba wa-ushfiqu ʿalayhimā wa-humā yaʿrifāni anna mā lī dhanbun fī ḍarbihimā wa-yaqbalāni ʿudhrī
sentences.l: So I did not cease, O commander of the believers, beating the two of them that beating, and pitying them, while the two of them know that there is not to me any fault in their beating, and accept my excuse.
sentences.i: So, Commander of the Faithful, I have gone on beating them like that, and pitying them all the while; and they know that I am not to blame for beating them, and they accept my excuse.
sentences.n: أَنَّ مَا لِي ذَنْبٌ, literally 'that not to me a fault', means 'that I have no fault'; مَا negates a noun sentence, as often in Middle Arabic. أَشْفَقَ عَلَيْهِ 'to pity him' takes عَلَى.

sentences.t: وَهَذِةِ قِصَّتِي وَحِكَايَتِي
sentences.tr: wa-hādhihi qiṣṣatī wa-ḥikāyatī
sentences.l: And this is my story and my tale.
sentences.i: That is my story and my tale.
sentences.n: هَذِةِ is the edition's spelling of هَذِهِ (ة for ه); it is read hādhihi.

sentences.t: قَالَ صَاحِبُ الْحِكَايَةِ فَتَعَجَّبَ الْخَلِيفَةُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: qāla ṣāḥibu al-ḥikāyati fa-taʿajjaba al-khalīfatu min dhālika
sentences.l: The teller of the tale said: And the caliph marvelled at that.
sentences.i: The teller of the tale says: The caliph marvelled at this.
sentences.n: صَاحِبُ الْحِكَايَةِ 'the owner of the tale' is the narrator's formula for himself, breaking in from outside the story.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لِلصَّبِيَّةِ الثَّانِيَةِ وَأَنْتِ مَا سَبَبُ الضَّرْبِ الَّذِي عَلَى جَسَدِكِ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla li-al-ṣabiyyati al-thāniyati wa-anti mā sababu al-ḍarbi alladhī ʿalā jasadiki
sentences.l: Then he said to the second girl: And you, what is the cause of the beating which is upon your body?
sentences.i: Then he said to the second girl, "And you: what is the cause of the beating that marks your body?"
sentences.n: وَأَنْتِ 'and you' turns the question to the second lady, after the first; وَ is not 'and' in the sense of addition, but 'as for you'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِنِّي كَانَ لِي وَالِدٌ فَتُوُفِّيَ وَخَلَّفَ مَالًا كَثِيرًا فَأَقَمْتُ بَعْدَهُ مُدَّةً يَسِيرَةً وَتَزَوَّجْتُ بِرَجُلٍ أَسْعَدِ أَهْلِ زَمَانِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat yā amīra al-muʾminīna innī kāna lī wālidun fa-tuwuffiya wa-khallafa mālan kathīran fa-aqamtu baʿdahu muddatan yasīratan wa-tazawwajtu bi-rajulin asʿadi ahli zamānihi
sentences.l: So she said: O commander of the believers, indeed I, there was to me a father, and he died, and left behind much wealth; and I stayed after him a short time, and married a man, the happiest of the people of his time.
sentences.i: She said, "Commander of the Faithful, I had a father, who died and left much wealth. I stayed on after him a short while, and then I married a man, the most fortunate of the men of his time.
sentences.n: تَزَوَّجْتُ بِرَجُلٍ 'I married a man': تَزَوَّجَ takes بِـ (or directly its object) for the husband; here it links the verb with the man. Note the shift of speaker: from here the second lady tells her own tale.

sentences.t: فَأَقَمْتُ مَعَهُ سَنَةً وَمَاتَ فَوَرِثْتُ مِنْهُ ثَمَانِينَ أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ ذَهَبٍ وَهِيَ حِصَّتِي بِالْفَرِيضَةِ الشَّرْعِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-aqamtu maʿahu sanatan wa-māta fa-warithtu minhu thamānīna alfa dīnārin dhahabin wa-hiya ḥiṣṣatī bi-al-farīḍati al-sharʿiyyati
sentences.l: So I stayed with him a year, and he died, and I inherited from him eighty thousand dinars of gold, and it was my share by the legal ordinance.
sentences.i: I lived with him a year, and he died; I inherited eighty thousand gold dinars from him, which was my share under the law of inheritance.
sentences.n: بِالْفَرِيضَةِ الشَّرْعِيَّةِ 'by the legal ordinance': الْفَرِيضَة is the fixed share of an heir laid down by the sharia, and بِـ names the basis, 'according to'. وَرِثَ مِنْهُ 'to inherit from him' takes مِنْ for the deceased.

sentences.t: وَفُقْتُ فِي السَّعَادَةِ وَشَاعَ خَبَرِي فَعَمِلْتُ عَشْرَ بَدَلَاتٍ كُلَّ بَدْلَةٍ بِأَلْفِ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: wa-fuqtu fī al-saʿādati wa-shāʿa khabarī fa-ʿamiltu ʿashra badalātin kulla badlatin bi-alfi dīnārin
sentences.l: And I excelled in happiness, and my report spread, and I had made ten suits, each suit at a thousand dinars.
sentences.i: I surpassed all in good fortune, and word of me spread. I had ten suits of clothes made, each suit worth a thousand dinars.
sentences.n: عَمِلْتُ 'I made (had made)' takes the suits as object. بِأَلْفِ دِينَارٍ 'at a thousand dinars': بِـ gives the price.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا أَنَا جَالِسَةٌ فِي يَوْمٍ مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ إِذْ دَخَلَتْ عَلَيَّ عَجُوزٌ بِخَدٍّ مَشْمُوطٍ وَحَاجِبٍ مَمْقُوطٍ وَعُيُونٍ مُغْبَرَّةٍ وَأَسْنَانٍ مُكَسَّرَةٍ وَوَجْهٍ أَنْمَشَ وَلَحْظٍ أَعْمَشَ وَرَأْسٍ مُجَصَّصٍ وَشَعْرٍ أَشْهَبَ وَجِسْمٍ أَجْرَبَ وَقَلٍّ مَائِلٍ وَلَوْنٍ حَائِلٍ وَمُخَاطٍ سَائِلٍ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā anā jālisatun fī yawmin mina al-ayyāmi idh dakhalat ʿalayya ʿajūzun bi-khaddin mashmūṭin wa-ḥājibin mamqūṭin wa-ʿuyūnin mughbarratin wa-asnānin mukassaratin wa-wajhin anmasha wa-laḥẓin aʿmasha wa-raʾsin mujaṣṣaṣin wa-shaʿrin ashhaba wa-jismin ajraba wa-qallin māʾilin wa-lawnin ḥāʾilin wa-mukhāṭin sāʾilin
sentences.l: So while I was sitting one day of the days, when there entered upon me an old woman, with a cheek plucked-and-streaked, and a brow plucked-out, and eyes dust-covered, and teeth broken, and a face freckled, and a glance bleary, and a head plastered-white, and hair grizzled, and a body mangy, and a stature stooped, and a colour faded, and snot running.
sentences.i: One day, as I sat at home, an old woman came in to me, with a blotched cheek and a plucked brow, dusty eyes and broken teeth, a freckled face and a bleary gaze, a whitewashed head and grizzled hair, a mangy body, a stooping frame, a faded hue, and snot running.
sentences.n: This is a list of rhymed ugliness, each phrase built as بِـ + a noun + an adjective ending in -ā-ʾil or -ūṭ, and the sajʿ falls on the last syllables. Each بِـ and وَ introduces a further feature of the old woman: 'with (having) a cheek...'. The meanings of مَشْمُوطٍ and مَمْقُوطٍ are uncertain; ممقوط seems to mean 'plucked of hair' and مشموط 'streaked, blotched' but both are unsure. مُجَصَّصٍ is 'plastered with gypsum', i.e. chalk-white with age or lime. The edition prints قل, and قَلٍّ is kept as printed; it is best read as a slip for قَدٍّ 'stature', matching مَائِلٍ 'leaning, stooped'. إِذْ after بَيْنَمَا 'while... when' introduces the sudden event.

sentences.t: كَمَا قَالَ فِيهَا الْقَائِلُ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: ka-mā qāla fīhā al-qāʾilu shiʿrun
sentences.l: As the sayer said of her: verse.
sentences.i: As the poet has said of such a one:
sentences.n: كَمَا is 'as', كَـ + مَا; here it opens a quotation. شِعْر is the edition's heading marking that verse follows.

sentences.t:
عَجُوزُ النَّحْسِ لَا يُرْحَمُ صِبَاهَا * وَلَا يُغْفَرُ لَهَا يَوْمًا تَمُوتُ
تَقُودُ مِنَ السِّيَاسَةِ أَلْفَ بَغْلٍ * إِذَا نَفَرُوا بِخَيْطِ الْعَنْكَبُوتِ
sentences.tr:
ʿajūzu al-naḥsi lā yurḥamu ṣibāhā * wa-lā yughfaru lahā yawman tamūtu
taqūdu mina al-siyāsati alfa baghlin * idhā nafarū bi-khaywi al-ʿankabūti
sentences.l:
The hag of ill-luck: her youth is not pitied * and it is not forgiven her, a day she dies,
She leads, out of statecraft, a thousand mules * when they bolt at a spider's thread.
sentences.i: Ah, the hag of ill luck! No pity is shown to her youth, and no pardon to her on the day she dies. Such is her cunning that she could lead a thousand mules, though they bolt at a spider's thread.
sentences.n: The first line is obscure and I have vocalised it as two passives, taking the youth (صِبَاهَا) as that of the hag's victim or of the hag herself; either reading is only a guess, and the words may be corrupt. The point of the couplet is the old go-between's power: مِنَ السِّيَاسَةِ 'out of statecraft' means she manages by cunning what force could not.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلَتِ الْعَجُوزُ سَلَّمَتْ عَلَيَّ وَبَاسَتِ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ وَقَالَتْ لِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhalati al-ʿajūzu sallamat ʿalayya wa-bāsati al-arḍa bayna yadayya wa-qālat lī
sentences.l: So when the old woman entered, she greeted me and kissed the ground between my two hands and said to me:
sentences.i: When the old woman came in, she greeted me, kissed the ground before me, and said to me:
sentences.n: بَاسَ (yabūsu) is the everyday word for 'kiss' in Middle Arabic, where Classical Arabic prefers قَبَّلَ; you will meet both in this night, and it is kept as printed.

sentences.t: عِنْدِي بِنْتٌ يَتِيمَةٌ وَاللَّيْلَةَ عَمِلْتُ عُرْسَهَا وَجِلَاهَا وَنَحْنُ غُرَبَاءُ فِي هَٰذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَلَا نَعْرِفُ أَحَدًا مِنْ أَهْلِهَا وَقَدِ انْكَسَرَتْ قُلُوبُنَا
sentences.tr: ʿindī bintun yatīmatun wa-al-laylata ʿamiltu ʿursahā wa-jilāhā wa-naḥnu ghurabāʾu fī hādhihi al-madīnati wa-lā naʿrifu aḥadan min ahlihā wa-qadi inkasarat qulūbunā
sentences.l: With me is an orphan girl, and tonight I made her wedding and her bridal-display, and we are strangers in this city and do not know anyone of its people, and our hearts have been broken.
sentences.i: I have an orphan girl in my care, and tonight I am holding her wedding and her bridal display. We are strangers in this city and know no one of its people, and our hearts are broken.
sentences.n: جِلَاهَا is read as the 'unveiling' or public display of the bride (jilwa); the printed spelling has no hamza after the alif, so the exact form is a guess, but the sense is clear from the wedding context. عِنْدِي 'with me' is the ordinary way of saying 'I have'.

sentences.t: فَارْجِى الْأَجْرَ وَالثَّوَابَ بِأَنَّكِ تَحْضُرِي جِلَاهَا حَتَّى تَسْمَعُوا اسِتَّاتُ مَدِينَتِنَا بِأَنَّكِ حَضَرْتِي فَيَحْضُرْنَ فَتَكُونِي جَبْرَةَ خَاطِرِهَا فَإِنَّهَا مَكْسُورَةُ الْخَاطِرِ لَيْسَ لَهَا إِلَّا اللَّهُ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: fa-irjī al-ajra wa-al-thawāba bi-annaki taḥḍurī jilāhā ḥattā tasmaʿū sittātu madīnatinā bi-annaki ḥaḍartī fa-yaḥḍurna fa-takūnī jabrata khāṭirihā fa-innahā maksūratu al-khāṭiri laysa lahā illā Allāhu taʿālā
sentences.l: So hope for the reward and the recompense by that-you attend her display, until they hear, the ladies of our city, that you have attended, so that they attend, and you be the mending of her heart; for she is broken of heart; she has none but God, exalted.
sentences.i: So look for reward and recompense in attending her display, so that the ladies of our city may hear that you have come and come themselves, and you will have mended her heart. For she is broken-hearted and has no one but God, the Exalted.
sentences.n: Several Middle Arabic habits meet here. The final -na is dropped in تَحْضُرِي and فَتَكُونِي, where Classical Arabic would have تَحْضُرِينَ and the subjunctive فَتَكُونِي only after certain particles; حَضَرْتِي carries a long -ī that the Classical form lacks; and تَسْمَعُوا is a plural verb standing before its noun. اسِتَّاتُ is read as سِتَّاتُ 'ladies' (from sitt, 'lady') with a stray initial alif. فَارْجِى may be the imperative 'hope for!' as read here, or 'I hope for' (أَرْجُو) spelled with ى; the sense is nearly the same.

sentences.t: وَبَكَتْ وَقَبَّلَتْ رِجْلَيَّ وَجَعَلَتْ تَقُولُ هَٰذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: wa-bakat wa-qabbalat rijlayya wa-jaʿalat taqūlu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: And she wept, and kissed my two feet, and began to say these verses:
sentences.i: Then she wept, kissed my feet, and began to recite these verses:

sentences.t:
حُضُورُكُمْ لَنَا شَرَفٌ * وَنَحْنُ بِذَٰلِكَ نَعْتَرِفُ
فَإِنْ غِبْتُمْ عَنَّا فَلَا عِوَضٌ * لَنَا وَلَا خَلَفٌ
sentences.tr:
ḥuḍūrukum lanā sharafun * wa-naḥnu bi-dhālika naʿtarifu
fa-in ghibtum ʿannā fa-lā ʿiwaḍun * lanā wa-lā khalafun
sentences.l:
Your presence is an honour for us * and we acknowledge it;
But if you are absent from us, there is no compensation * for us and no successor.
sentences.i: Your coming is an honour to us, and this we freely own; but if you stay away, there is no recompense for us, and no one to take your place.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَتْنِي الرَّحْمَةُ وَالرَّأْفَةُ فَقُلْتُ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً وَقُلْتُ لَهَا أَنَا أَعْمَلُ مَعَهَا شَيْءٌ مَعَ مَشِيئَةِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى وَمَا أُجَلِّيهَا إِلَّا بِحُلَلِي وَمَصَاغِي وَ تَرَاكِبِي
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhatnī al-raḥmatu wa-al-raʾfatu fa-qultu samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan wa-qultu lahā anā aʿmalu maʿahā shayʾun maʿa mashīʾati Allāhi taʿālā wa-mā ajallīhā illā bi-ḥulalī wa-maṣāghī wa tarākibī
sentences.l: And mercy and compassion took me, so I said: with hearing and obedience; and I said to her: I, I will do something with her, with the will of God, exalted, and I shall not display her except in my robes and my jewellery and my settings.
sentences.i: Pity and tenderness took hold of me, and I said, with hearing and obedience. I told her that I would do something for the girl, God willing, and that I would present her in none but my own robes, jewels and ornaments.
sentences.n: شَيْءٌ is left in the nominative, as printed; Classical Arabic would want the accusative شَيْئًا after أَعْمَلُ. The last word, تَرَاكِبِي, is uncertain: I take it as a plural of a word for jewel-settings or fittings (perhaps تَرْكِيبَة), but the reading is a guess. Note too the edition's stray وَ before it, kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَتِ الْعَجُوزُ وَطَأْطَأَتْ عَلَى رِجْلَيَّ تُقَبِّلُهُمْ وَقَالَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥati al-ʿajūzu wa-ṭaʾṭaʾat ʿalā rijlayya tuqabbiluhum wa-qālat
sentences.l: So the old woman rejoiced and bowed down upon my two feet, kissing them, and said:
sentences.i: The old woman was overjoyed. She bent low over my feet, kissing them, and said:
sentences.n: رِجْلَيَّ is 'my two feet' but is picked up by the plural pronoun هُمْ; Middle Arabic often lets a dual noun be referred to as a plural.

sentences.t: اللَّهُ يُجَازِيكِ خَيْرًا وَيَجْبُرُ قَلْبَكِ مِثْلَ مَا جَبَرْتِ قَلْبِي
sentences.tr: Allāhu yujāzīki khayran wa-yajburu qalbaki mithla mā jabartī qalbī
sentences.l: God repays you good and mends your heart, the like of what you mended my heart.
sentences.i: May God reward you well and mend your heart as you have mended mine.
sentences.n: The bare imperfect (اللَّهُ يُجَازِيكِ) is a wish, the everyday way of saying 'may God ...'. The same verb, جَبَرَ 'to mend' (as a bone is set), returns as جَبْرَة 'a mending' in the old woman's first speech.

sentences.t: وَلَٰكِنْ سَيِّدَتِي لَا تَكَلَّفِي خِدْمَتَكِ مِنْ هَٰذَا الْوَقْتِ وَلَٰكِنْ تَجَهَّزِي لِلْعَشَاءِ حَتَّى أَجِيءَ آخُذَكِ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin sayyidatī lā takallafī khidmataki min hādhā al-waqti wa-lākin tajahhazī li-al-ʿashāʾi ḥattā ajīʾa ākhudhaki
sentences.l: But, my lady, do not burden-yourself-with your service from this time; but make-yourself-ready for the supper until I come, take you.
sentences.i: But, my lady, do not trouble yourself with serving us from this hour; only make ready for the evening, and I will come and fetch you.
sentences.n: The first clause is not fully clear. I take تَكَلَّفِي (Form V, 'put yourself to trouble over') with خِدْمَتَكِ as 'do not go to the trouble of attending upon us yet'. Note also أَجِيءَ آخُذَكِ 'I come, take you' with no 'and', a Middle Arabic run-on.

sentences.t: وَبَاسَتْ يَدَيَّ وَذَهَبَتْ فَقُمْتُ عَلَّنْتُ نَفْسِي وَحَالِي وَإِذَا بِالْعَجُوزِ قَدْ أَقْبَلَتْ وَقَالَتْ
sentences.tr: wa-bāsat yadayya wa-dhahabat fa-qumtu ʿallantu nafsī wa-ḥālī wa-idhā bi-al-ʿajūzi qad aqbalat wa-qālat
sentences.l: And she kissed my two hands and went off; so I rose, I-ʿallantu myself and my state, and behold, the old woman had come forward, and she said:
sentences.i: She kissed my hands and left. I got up and set myself and my affairs in order, and behold, the old woman was back, and she said:
sentences.n: عَلَّنْتُ is obscure. It may be a misprint, or a garbled form of a verb for 'make ready, put in order' (perhaps عَمِلْتُ or a dialect word), and I have read it as Form II of عَلَنَ 'to make plain'; the sense 'I got ready' is what the context asks for. The verbs فَقُمْتُ عَلَّنْتُ follow without 'and', another Middle Arabic run-on. وَإِذَا بِـ ('and behold') is the surprise formula: the بِـ merely marks what appears.

sentences.t: يَا سَيِّدَتِي إِنَّ سِتَّاتِ الْبَلَدِ قَدْ حَضَرْنَ وَ أَخْبَرْتُهُمْ بِحُضُورِكِ فَفَرِحُوا وَهُمْ فِي انْتِظَارِكِ مُتَطَلِّعِينَ قُدُومَكِ
sentences.tr: yā sayyidatī inna sittāti al-baladi qad ḥaḍarna wa akhbartuhum bi-ḥuḍūriki fa-fariḥū wa-hum fī intiẓāriki mutaṭalliʿīna qudūmaki
sentences.l: O my lady, the ladies of the town have attended, and I informed them of your attending, and they rejoiced, and they are in waiting-for-you, looking-out for your coming.
sentences.i: My lady, the ladies of the town have come. I told them you would be attending, and they were delighted; they are waiting for you, watching eagerly for your arrival.
sentences.n: The plural masculine فَفَرِحُوا and هُمْ refer to women, where Classical Arabic would use the feminine (فَفَرِحْنَ, هُنَّ), while حَضَرْنَ just before is properly feminine; Middle Arabic mixes the two.

sentences.t: وَ تَأَزَّرْتُ فَقُمْتُ وَأَخَذْتُ جَوَارِيَ مَعِي وَسِرْتُ حَتَّى أَتَيْنَا إِلَى زُقَاقٍ مَكْنُوسٍ مَرْشُوشٍ هَبَّ فِيهِ النَّسِيمُ وَرَاقَ
sentences.tr: wa taʾazzartu fa-qumtu wa-akhadhtu jawāriya maʿī wa-sirtu ḥattā ataynā ilā zuqāqin maknūsin marshūshin habba fīhi al-nasīmu wa-rāqa
sentences.l: And I wrapped-myself-in-the-izār, and I rose and took my slave-girls with me and went on until we came to an alley, swept, sprinkled, in which the breeze blew, and it was pleasant.
sentences.i: I wrapped myself in my izar, rose, took my maids with me, and walked on until we came to an alley, swept and sprinkled with water, where the breeze blew softly and all was pleasant.
sentences.n: The edition prints a stray وَ at the end of the previous line, apart from the word it belongs to; it is kept here as a separate word. تَأَزَّرَ is 'to put on the izār', the large outer wrap women wore in the street. Sprinkling the ground with water to lay the dust is still a sign of a house prepared for guests.

sentences.t: فَقَدِمْنَا إِلَى بَابٍ مُقَنْطَرٍ بِقُبَّةٍ مِنَ الرُّخَامِ شَدِيدَةِ الْبُنْيَانِ عَلَى بَابِ الْقَصْرِ قَدْ قَامَ مِنَ التُّرَابِ وَ تَعَلَّقَ بِالسَّحَابِ مَكْتُوبٌ عَلَى الْبَابِ هَٰذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتُ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qadimnā ilā bābin muqanṭarin bi-qubbatin mina al-rukhāmi shadīdati al-bunyāni ʿalā bābi al-qaṣri qad qāma mina al-turābi wa taʿallaqa bi-al-saḥābi maktūbun ʿalā al-bābi hādhihi al-abyātu shiʿrun
sentences.l: So we came to a gate, arched with a dome of marble, strong of structure, upon the gate of the palace, which had risen from the dust and hung to the clouds; written on the gate: these verses. Verse:
sentences.i: We came to a gate arched over with a dome of marble, massively built, the gate of the palace; it had risen from the dust and clung to the clouds. On the gate these verses were written:
sentences.n: The gate is described in the stock language of sajʿ: it 'rose from the dust and hung to the clouds'. The stray وَ before تَعَلَّقَ is the edition's, kept as printed.

sentences.t:
أَنَا دَارٌ بُنِيتُ لِلْأَفْرَاحِ * طُولَ دَهْرِي لِلْبَسْطِ وَالِانْشِرَاحِ
وَبِوَسْطِي فَسْقِيَّةٌ تَتَدَفَّقُ * بِمِيَاهٍ تُزِيلُ بِالْأَتْرَاحِ
وَعَلَيْهَا مِنَ الشَّقِيقِ زُهُورُ * وَرْدٍ آسٍ وَنَرْجِسٍ وَأُقَاحِ
sentences.tr:
anā dārun bunītu li-al-afrāḥi * ṭūla dahrī li-al-basṭi wa-al-inshirāḥi
wa-bi-wasṭī fasqiyyatun tatadaffaqu * bi-miyāhin tuzīlu bi-al-atrāḥi
wa-ʿalayhā mina al-shaqīqi zuhūru * wardin āsin wa-narjisin wa-uqāḥi
sentences.l:
I am a house built for joys * all the length of my age for expansion and gladness,
And in my middle a basin gushing * with waters that remove griefs,
And upon it, of anemones, flowers * of rose, myrtle, narcissus and camomile.
sentences.i: I am a house built for delights, given all my days to mirth and gladness. In my midst a fountain gushes with waters that drive griefs away, and about it bloom anemones, roses, myrtle, narcissus and camomile.
sentences.n: The house speaks in the first person. In the second couplet the بِـ before الْأَتْرَاحِ is odd (تُزِيلُ takes a direct object); I read it as a loose 'with', so the waters 'remove griefs'. In the third I have taken زُهُورُ as the first word of an annexation, 'flowers of rose, myrtle ...', so that the line can end on the rhyme in -ḥi, and the list is left without 'and' between وَرْدٍ and آسٍ as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَصَلْنَا إِلَى الْبَابِ طَرَقَتْهُ الْعَجُوزُ فَفُتِحَ لَنَا وَدَخَلْنَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waṣalnā ilā al-bābi ṭaraqathu al-ʿajūzu fa-futiḥa lanā wa-dakhalnā
sentences.l: So when we reached the gate, the old woman knocked it, and it was opened for us, and we entered.
sentences.i: When we reached the gate, the old woman knocked, it was opened to us, and we went in.

sentences.t: فَوَجَدْنَا دِهْلِيزًا مَفْرُوشًا بِالْبُسُطِ وَمُعَلَّقٌ فِيهِ قَنَادِيلُ مَوْقُودَةٌ وَشُمُوعٌ مَصْفُوفَةٌ فِيهَا الْجَوَاهِرُ وَالْمَعَادِنُ
sentences.tr: fa-wajadnā dihlīzan mafrūshan bi-al-busuṭi wa-muʿallaqun fīhi qanādīlu mawqūdatun wa-shumūʿun maṣfūfatun fīhā al-jawāhiru wa-al-maʿādinu
sentences.l: And we found a vestibule, spread with the carpets, and hung in it lamps, lit, and candles, set-in-rows, in them the jewels and the metals.
sentences.i: Inside we found a vestibule spread with carpets, hung with burning lamps and lined with candles set out in rows, in candlesticks of jewels and precious metals.
sentences.n: وَمُعَلَّقٌ is left nominative as printed, where Classical Arabic would continue the accusative (وَمُعَلَّقًا). The candles' 'in them the jewels and metals' probably describes their holders; the printed phrase is elliptical.

sentences.t: فَمَشَيْنَا مِنَ الدِّهْلِيزِ إِلَى أَنْ دَخَلْنَا قَاعَةً لَا يُوجَدُ لَهَا نَظِيرٌ مَفْرُوشَةً بِالْفِرَاشِ الْحَرِيرِ مُعَلَّقٌ فِيهَا الْقَنَادِيلُ مَوْقُودَةً وَ الشُّمُوعُ صَفَّيْنِ وَفِي صَدْرِ الْقَاعَةِ سَرِيرٌ مِنَ الْعَرْعَرِ مُرَصَّعٌ بِالدُّرِّ وَ الْجَوْهَرِ
sentences.tr: fa-mashaynā mina al-dihlīzi ilā an dakhalnā qāʿatan lā yūjadu lahā naẓīrun mafrūshatan bi-al-firāshi al-ḥarīri muʿallaqun fīhā al-qanādīlu mawqūdatan wa al-shumūʿu saffayni wa-fī ṣadri al-qāʿati sarīrun mina al-ʿarʿari muraṣṣaʿun bi-al-durri wa al-jawhari
sentences.l: So we walked from the vestibule until we entered a hall, no equal to it is found, spread with the silk bedding, hung in it the lamps, lit, and the candles in two rows; and in the upper part of the hall a couch of juniper-wood, studded with pearls and jewels.
sentences.i: We walked on from the vestibule until we entered a hall without its equal, spread with silken carpets and hung with burning lamps, and the candles stood in two rows. At the head of the hall was a couch of juniper wood, studded with pearls and gems,
sentences.n: الْعَرْعَر is juniper, a fragrant, costly wood. The two stray وَ before الشُّمُوعُ and الْجَوْهَرِ are the edition's line-break slips, kept as printed. لَا يُوجَدُ لَهَا نَظِيرٌ 'no equal is found for it' is a stock phrase for a hall without rival.

sentences.t: وَعَلَيْهِ بَشْخَانَةُ أَطْلَسٍ مُزَرَّرٍ وَلَمْ نَشْعُرْ حَتَّى خَرَجَتْ صَبِيَّةٌ مِنَ الْبَشْخَانَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿalayhi bashkhānatu aṭlasin muzarrarin wa-lam nashʿur ḥattā kharajat ṣabiyyatun mina al-bashkhānati
sentences.l: And over it a bashkhāna of satin, buttoned; and we did not perceive until a girl came out from the bashkhāna.
sentences.i: and above it a canopy of buttoned satin. We had noticed nothing when a young girl came out from under the canopy.
sentences.n: بَشْخَانَة is a curtained canopy or pavilion (from Persian pīshkhāna); I take مُزَرَّر as 'fastened with loops or buttons'. The reading is a best guess from the context.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرْتُ إِلَيْهَا يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فَإِذَا هِيَ أَكْمَلُ مِنَ الْبَدْرِ إِذَا بَدَرَ بِجَبِينٍ أَزْهَرَ كَالصُّبْحِ إِذَا أَسْفَرَ كَمَا قَالَ الشَّاعِرُ حَيْثُ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓartu ilayhā yā amīra al-muʾminīna fa-idhā hiya akmalu mina al-badri idhā badara bi-jabīnin azhara ka-al-ṣubḥi idhā asfara ka-mā qāla al-shāʿiru ḥaythu yaqūlu
sentences.l: So I looked at her, O commander of the believers, and behold, she was more perfect than the full moon when it comes-to-fullness, with a radiant forehead, like the dawn when it brightens, as the poet said, where he says:
sentences.i: I looked at her, Commander of the Faithful, and there she was, more perfect than the full moon in its fullness, with a brow as radiant as the daybreak when it shines forth, just as the poet says:
sentences.n: الْبَدْر ('the full moon') and بَدَرَ ('it came to fullness') play on one root. The narrator turns aside to the caliph here (يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ), as the whole tale is told to him. Here فَإِذَا هِيَ 'and behold, she' is the surprise formula.

sentences.t:
أَنْتِ عَلَى الْقَصَرَاتِ الْقَيْصَرِيَّاتِ * خُودٌ مِنَ الْخَفِرَاتِ الْكِسْرَوِيَّاتِ
تَبْدُو دَلَائِلُ خَدَّيْهَا مُوَرَّدَةً * يَاحُسْنَ تِلْكَ الْخُدُودِ الْعَنْدَمِيَّاتِ
هَيْفَاءُ فَاتِرَةُ الْأَلْحَاظِ نَاعِسَةٌ * حَازَتْ مِنَ الْحُسْنِ أَنْوَاعَ الْمَلَاحَاتِ
كَأَنَّ طُرَّتَهَا مِنْ فَوْقِ غُرَّتِهَا * لَيْلُ الْهُمُومِ عَلَيٰ صُبْحِ الْمَسَرَّاتِ
sentences.tr:
anti ʿalā al-qaṣarāti al-qayṣariyyāti * khūdun mina al-khafirāti al-kisrawiyyāti
tabdū dalāʾilu khaddayhā muwarradatan * yā ḥusna tilka al-khudūdi al-ʿandamiyyāti
hayfāʾu fātiratu al-alḥāẓi nāʿisatun * ḥāzat mina al-ḥusni anwāʿa al-malāḥāti
ka-anna ṭurratahā min fawqi ghurratihā * laylu al-humūmi ʿalā ṣubḥi al-masarrāti
sentences.l:
You, upon the qaṣarāt, the Caesarean-ones, * a lissom girl of the modest-ones, the Chosroan-ones,
The tokens of her two cheeks appear rose-tinted * O the beauty of those cheeks, the dragon's-blood-red ones,
Slender-waisted, languid of glances, drowsy, * she has won, of beauty, kinds of comeliness,
As if her forelock above her blaze * were the night of cares upon the morning of joys.
sentences.i: You, standing among Caesar's halls, are a slender girl of the modest maidens of Chosroes' line; the tokens of her cheeks show rosy, ah, the beauty of those cheeks, red as dragon's blood! Slender of waist, languid of glance and drowsy-eyed, she has won every kind of loveliness; and her forelock above her brow is like the night of cares laid over the morning of joys.
sentences.n: The first line is obscure. I read الْقَصَرَات as a plural of قَصْر 'palace', but the word is also found for 'necks' and I cannot be certain; 'Caesarean' and 'Chosroan' (Roman and Persian) simply mean 'princely, of the grandest sort'. Some of the words carry a stray spelling: the last hemistich prints عَلَيٰ for عَلَىٰ (ʿalā, 'upon'), a Middle Arabic slip kept as printed and given the dagger alif. عَنْدَم is dragon's blood, a red dye; الْعَنْدَمِيَّات 'the dragon's-blood-red ones' means 'flushed'.

sentences.t: فَنَزَلَتِ الصَّبِيَّةُ مِنَ الْبَشْخَانَةِ وَقَالَتْ لِي مَرْحَبًا وَأَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا بِالْأُخْتِ الْعَزِيزَةِ الْجَلِيلَةِ وَأَلْفَ مَرْحَبًا ثُمَّ أَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ هَٰذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-nazalati al-ṣabiyyatu mina al-bashkhānati wa-qālat lī marḥaban wa-ahlan wa-sahlan bi-al-ukhti al-ʿazīzati al-jalīlati wa-alfa marḥaban thumma anshadat taqūlu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: So the girl came down from the bashkhāna and said to me: welcome, and kinsfolk, and ease, to the dear, exalted sister, and a thousand welcomes; then she recited, saying, these verses:
sentences.i: The girl came down from the canopy and said to me: welcome, welcome and all ease to my dear and honoured sister, a thousand welcomes! Then she recited these verses:
sentences.n: مَرْحَبًا وَأَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا is the stock greeting, each word an accusative wish ('may you find room, kin and ease'); the بِـ before الْأُخْتِ names the person greeted.

sentences.t:
لَوْ تَعْلَمُ الدَّارُ مَنْ قَدْ زَارَهَا فَرِحَتْ * وَاسْتَبْشَرَتْ ثُمَّ بَاسَتْ مَوْضِعَ الْقَدَمِ
وَأَنْشَدَتْ بِلِسَانِ الْحَالِ قَائِلَةً * أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا بِأَهْلِ الْجُودِ وَالْكَرَمِ
sentences.tr:
law taʿlamu al-dāru man qad zārahā fariḥat * wa-istabsharat thumma bāsat mawḍiʿa al-qadami
wa-anshadat bi-lisāni al-ḥāli qāʾilatan * ahlan wa-sahlan bi-ahli al-jūdi wa-al-karami
sentences.l:
If the house knew who has visited it, it would rejoice * and be glad, then kiss the place of the foot,
And it would recite, with the tongue of its state, saying: * welcome and ease to the people of generosity and nobility.
sentences.i: Did the house but know who has come to visit it, it would rejoice and be glad, and kiss the very place where your foot has trod, and it would declare in the silent speech of its condition: welcome and ease to the people of bounty and nobility!
sentences.n: بِلِسَانِ الْحَالِ 'with the tongue of the state' is an idiom for saying something by one's plight rather than in words. Both past-tense verbs after لَوْ (فَرِحَتْ ... وَأَنْشَدَتْ) are conditional in sense, 'it would have rejoiced ...'.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ جَلَسَتْ وَقَالَتْ لِي
sentences.tr: thumma jalasat wa-qālat lī
sentences.l: Then she sat and said to me:
sentences.i: Then she sat down and said to me:

sentences.t: يَا أُخْتِي إِنَّ لِي أَخًا وَقَدْ رَأَكِ فِي بَعْضِ الْأَفْرَاحِ وَالْمَوَاسِمِ وَهُوَ شَابٌّ أَحْسَنُ مِنِّي
sentences.tr: yā ukhtī inna lī akhan wa-qad raʾaki fī baʿḍi al-afrāḥi wa-al-mawāsimi wa-huwa shābbun aḥsanu minnī
sentences.l: O my sister, I have a brother, and he has seen you at some of the weddings and festivals, and he is a youth more handsome than I.
sentences.i: Sister, I have a brother, who saw you at one of the weddings or festivals; he is a young man handsomer than I.
sentences.n: رَأَكِ is printed without the long vowel Classical Arabic has in رَآكِ; the edition's spelling is kept (and it is one of the words the edition itself prints with hamza). أَحْسَنُ مِنِّي 'more beautiful than I' is a comparative, with مِنْ 'than'.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ حَبَّكِ قَلْبُهُ حُبًّا شَدِيدًا لِأَنَّكِ حُزْتِ مِنَ الْحُسْنِ وَالْجَمَالِ أَوْفَى نَصِيبٍ وَسَمِعَ أَنَّكِ سَيِّدَةُ قَوْمِكِ وَهُوَ أَيْضًا سَيِّدُ قَوْمِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad ḥabbaki qalbuhu ḥubban shadīdan li-annaki ḥuzti mina al-ḥusni wa-al-jamāli awfā naṣībin wa-samiʿa annaki sayyidatu qawmiki wa-huwa aydan sayyidu qawmihi
sentences.l: And his heart has loved you with an intense love, because you have gained of beauty and comeliness the fullest share, and he heard that you are the lady of your people, and he too is the lord of his people.
sentences.i: His heart has loved you with a fierce love, because you have won the fullest share of beauty and grace; and he has heard that you are the lady of your people, and he too is the lord of his.
sentences.n: حَبَّكِ is the simple verb with a direct object, 'he loved you' (a spoken form; Classical would say أَحَبَّكِ), and I have vocalised it as printed.

sentences.t: فَأَرَادَ أَنْ يَصِلَ حَبْلَهُ بِحَبْلِكِ وَأَعْطَى هَٰذِهِ الْحِيلَةَ لِأَجْلِ اجْتِمَاعِي بِكِ وَيُرِيدُ يَتَزَوَّجُ بِكِ بِسُنَّةِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَمَا فِي الْحَلَالِ مِنْ عَيْبٍ
sentences.tr: fa-arāda an yaṣila ḥablahu bi-ḥablaki wa-aʿṭā hādhihi al-ḥīlata li-ajli ijtimāʿī bi-ki wa-yurīdu yatazawwaju bi-ki bi-sunnati Allāhi wa-rasūlihi wa-mā fī al-ḥalāli min ʿaybin
sentences.l: So he wished to join his rope with your rope, and he gave this ruse for the sake of my meeting with you; and he wants he marries with you by the custom of God and His messenger, and in the lawful is no fault.
sentences.i: So he wished to join his fortunes to yours, and he devised this stratagem so that I might meet you. He wants to marry you according to the law of God and His Messenger, and there is no blame in what is lawful.
sentences.n: Joining rope to rope is an image for a bond of kinship or alliance. وَأَعْطَى هَٰذِهِ الْحِيلَةَ is literally 'and gave this ruse'; I take it as 'contrived' but the wording is loose. يُرِيدُ يَتَزَوَّجُ 'he wants, he marries' has no أَنْ, a very common Middle Arabic pattern, and تَزَوَّجَ بِـ ('marry with') takes بِـ where Classical Arabic has a direct object.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ كَلَامَهَا وَرَأَيْتُ نَفْسِي قَدْ نَجَوَّبَتْ فِي الدَّارِ قُلْتُ لِلصَّبِيَّةِ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: qālat fa-lammā samiʿtu kalāmahā wa-raʾaytu nafsī qad najawwabat fī al-dāri qultu li-al-ṣabiyyati samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: She said: So when I heard her words and saw myself to have najawwabat in the house, I said to the girl: hearing and obedience.
sentences.i: She said: When I had heard her words, and saw that I was now well inside the house, I told the girl, with hearing and obedience.
sentences.n: نَجَوَّبَتْ is not a word I can identify: it may be a garbled spelling (perhaps of تَجَوَّبَتْ 'was entered, was pierced through', or of a verb meaning 'was shut in'). The clause is left as printed, and my English gives only the sense the context needs, that the narrator finds herself committed, inside the house. Note that نَفْسِي 'my self' takes a feminine verb.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَتْ وَصَفَّقَتْ عَلَى يَدَيْهَا وَفَتَحَتْ بَابًا وَخَرَجَ مِنْهُ شَابٌّ مَلِيحُ الشَّبَابِ نَقِيُّ الْأَثْوَابِ بِقَدٍّ وَاعْتِدَالٍ وَحُسْنٍ وَجَمَالٍ وَبَهَاءٍ وَكَمَالٍ وَرَخِيمُ الدَّلَالِ بِحَاجِبٍ كَقَوْسِ نَبَّالٍ وَعُيُونٍ تَخْتَلِسُ الْقُلُوبَ بِالسِّحْرِ الْحَلَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥat wa-ṣaffaqat ʿalā yadayhā wa-fataḥat bāban wa-kharaja minhu shābbun malīḥu al-shabābi naqiyyu al-athwābi bi-qaddin wa-iʿtidālin wa-ḥusnin wa-jamālin wa-bahāʾin wa-kamālin wa-rakhīmu al-dalāli bi-ḥājibin ka-qawsi nabbālin wa-ʿuyūnin takhtalisu al-qulūba bi-al-siḥri al-ḥalāli
sentences.l: So she rejoiced and clapped upon her hands and opened a door, and there came out from it a youth, fair of youth, clean of garments, with stature and evenness and beauty and comeliness and radiance and perfection, and soft of coquetry, with a brow like an archer's bow, and eyes that snatch the hearts with lawful magic.
sentences.i: She was delighted; she clapped her hands together and opened a door, and out came a young man, comely in his youth and spotless in his clothes, of graceful, even stature, beauty, comeliness, radiance and perfection, and tender in his airs, with a brow like an archer's bow and eyes that stole hearts with lawful sorcery.
sentences.n: The description runs in rhymed prose (sajʿ) on -āl, with a string of nouns after بِـ ('with stature, evenness, beauty ...'). I read رَخِيمُ الدَّلَالِ as one more adjective of the youth ('soft of coquetry'), and قَوْسِ نَبَّالٍ as 'an archer's bow'. السِّحْرُ الْحَلَالُ 'lawful magic' is a stock phrase for the charm of a beautiful glance, called lawful because it is not sorcery.

sentences.t: كَمَا قَالَ فِيهِ بَعْضُ وَاصِفِيهِ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: ka-mā qāla fīhi baʿḍu wāṣifīhi shiʿrun
sentences.l: As some of those-who-describe-him said in him: verse.
sentences.i: as one of those who described him has said of him in verse:

sentences.t: لَهُ وَجْهٌ كَوَجْهِ الْهِلَالِ * وَآثَارُ السَّعَادَةِ كَاللَّآلِي
sentences.tr: lahu wajhun ka-wajhi al-hilāli * wa-āthāru al-saʿādati ka-al-laʾālī
sentences.l: He has a face like the face of the crescent * and the traces of felicity like pearls.
sentences.i: His face is like the crescent moon, and the marks of good fortune on him gleam like pearls.
sentences.n: In كَوَجْهِ and كَاللَّآلِي the prefix كَـ means 'like', introducing each comparison.

sentences.t: وَأَيْضًا لِلَّهِ دَرُّ قَائِلِهِ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: wa-ayḍan lillāhi darru qāʾilihi shiʿr
sentences.l: And also: to God the flowing-of its sayer! Verse:
sentences.i: And again, how well its maker has spoken, in verse:
sentences.n: لِلَّهِ دَرُّهُ is a stock cry of praise, literally 'to God (belongs) his milk', that is, the rich flow of his gift; it means 'how well he has done!'

sentences.t:
تَبَارَكَ بِحُسْنٍ تَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ * جَلَّ الَّذِي صَاغَهُ وَسَوَّاهُ
قَدْ حَازَ كُلَّ الْجَمَالِ مُنْفَرِدًا * كُلُّ الْوَرَى فِي جَمَالِهِ تَاهُوا
قَدْ كَتَبَ الْحُسْنُ فَوْقَ وَجْنَتِهِ * أَشْهَدُأَنْ لَا مَلِيحَ إِلَّا هُوَ
sentences.tr:
tabāraka bi-ḥusnin tabāraka Allāhu * jalla al-ladhī ṣāghahu wa-sawwāhu
qad ḥāza kulla al-jamāli munfaridan * kullu al-warā fī jamālihi tāhū
qad kataba al-ḥusnu fawqa wajnatihi * ashhadu an lā malīḥa illā huwa
sentences.l:
Blessed is he in beauty, blessed be God! * Exalted is He who fashioned him and made him even.
He has gathered all beauty, alone in it; * all the created-ones, in his beauty, are lost.
Beauty has written upon his cheek: * I bear witness that there is no handsome one but he.
sentences.i: Blessed is he in his beauty, and blessed be God! Exalted is the One who moulded him and made him whole. He has gathered all loveliness to himself alone, and all mankind is lost in wonder at his beauty. Beauty has written upon his cheek: I bear witness that there is none fair but he.
sentences.n: The last line plays on the Muslim declaration of faith, 'I bear witness that there is no god but God', turning it into a declaration of the beloved's beauty. أَشْهَدُأَنْ is printed as one run, read أَشْهَدُ أَنْ 'I bear witness that'. The verse is otherwise printed bare and is pointed here.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرْتُ إِلَيْهِ مَالَ قَلْبِي لَهُ وَحَبَّبْتُهُ فَجَلَسَ بِجَانِبِي وَتَحَدَّثْتُ مَعَهُ سَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓartu ilayhi māla qalbī lahu wa-ḥabbabtuhu fa-jalasa bi-jānibī wa-taḥaddathtu maʿahu sāʿatan
sentences.l: So when I looked at him, my heart inclined to him, and I made-him-dear; and he sat at my side, and I talked with him an hour.
sentences.i: When I looked at him, my heart went out to him and I took a liking to him. He sat down beside me and I talked with him for an hour.
sentences.n: وَحَبَّبْتُهُ (form II) is 'I made him beloved', that is, 'I grew fond of him'.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ صَفَّقَتِ الصَّبِيَّةُ ثَانِي مَرَّةٍ وَإِذَا بِخُرَسْتَانٍ قَدِ انْفَتَحَ وَخَرَجَ مِنْهُ قَاضٍ وَمَعَهُ أَرْبَعُ شُهُودٍ
sentences.tr: thumma ṣaffaqati al-ṣabiyyatu thāniya marratin wa-idhā bi-khurastānin qadi infataḥa wa-kharaja minhu qāḍin wa-maʿahu arbaʿu shuhūdin
sentences.l: Then the girl clapped a second time, and behold, a closet had opened, and there came out of it a judge, and with him four witnesses.
sentences.i: Then the girl clapped her hands a second time, and behold, a cupboard-door opened and out of it stepped a judge with four witnesses.
sentences.n: وَإِذَا بِخُرَسْتَانٍ: the بِـ after إِذَا of surprise only marks what suddenly appears. خُرَسْتَان is a Persian-derived word for a cabinet or closet; the sense is a hidden door. أَرْبَعُ شُهُودٍ has no final ة on the number before a plural noun: Middle Arabic, kept as printed (Classical أَرْبَعَةُ شُهُودٍ).

sentences.t: فَسَلَّمُوا وَجَلَسُوا وَكَتَبْتُ الْكِتَابَ عَلَى الشَّابِّ وَ انْصَرَفُوا
sentences.tr: fa-sallamū wa-jalasū wa-katabtu al-kitāba ʿalā al-shābbi wa-inṣarafū
sentences.l: So they greeted, and sat, and I wrote the writing upon the youth, and they went away.
sentences.i: They gave their greeting and sat down; the marriage-contract was written between the youth and me, and then they departed.
sentences.n: وَكَتَبْتُ is printed with ت and so reads 'I wrote'; the sense is that the marriage contract was drawn up ('كَتَبَ الْكِتَابَ عَلَى' is the idiom for binding a man to a marriage contract). A reading 'they wrote' (وَكَتَبُوا) is what one expects, but the printed letters say 'I', and that is what is pointed here. The stray وَ before انْصَرَفُوا is the edition's own spacing, kept.

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتَ الشَّابُّ إِلَيَّ وَقَالَ لِي لَيْلَةٌ مُبَارَكَةٌ ثُمَّ قَالَ يَا سَيِّدَتِي أَشْرِطُ عَلَيْكِ شَرْطًا فَقُلْتُ يَا سَيِّدِي وَمَا الشَّرْطُ
sentences.tr: fa-iltafata al-shābbu ilayya wa-qāla lī laylatun mubārakatun thumma qāla yā sayyidatī ashriṭu ʿalayki sharṭan fa-qultu yā sayyidī wa-mā al-sharṭu
sentences.l: So the youth turned to me and said to me, A blessed night; then he said, O my lady, I lay upon you a condition. And I said, O my lord, and what is the condition?
sentences.i: The youth turned to me and said, A blessed night to you. Then he said, My lady, I lay one condition upon you. And I said, My lord, what is the condition?

sentences.t: فَقَامَ وَأَحْضَرَ لِي مُصْحَفًا وَقَالَ احْلِفِي أَنَّكِ لَاتَنْظُرِي أَحَدًا غَيْرِي وَلَا تَمِيلِي إِلَيْهِ فَحَلَفْتُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma wa-aḥḍara lī muṣḥafan wa-qāla iḥlifī annaki lātanẓurī aḥadan ghayrī wa-lā tamīlī ilayhi fa-ḥalaftu ʿalā dhālika
sentences.l: So he rose and brought me a Qurʾan-codex and said, Swear that you do not look at anyone other than me, and do not incline to him; and I swore to that.
sentences.i: He got up and fetched me a copy of the Qurʾan and said, Swear that you will look at no man but me, and turn to none other. And I swore to it.
sentences.n: لَاتَنْظُرِي and تَمِيلِي end in -ī with no final ن: a woman addressed in the present is dropping the -na of Classical تَنْظُرِينَ, a common Middle Arabic habit that recurs below. لَاتَنْظُرِي is printed as one run.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ فَرَحًا شَدِيدًا وَعَانَقَنِي فَأَخَذَتْ مَحَبَّتُهُ مَجَامِعَ قَلْبِي وَقَدَّمُوا لَنَا السِّمَاطَ فَأَكَلْنَا وَشَرِبْنَا حَتَّى اكْتَفَيْنَا وَدَخَلَ عَلَيْنَا فَأَخَذَنِي وَدَخَلَ إِلَى الْفِرَاشِ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa faraḥan shadīdan wa-ʿānaqanī fa-akhadhat maḥabbatuhu majāmiʿa qalbī wa-qaddamū lanā al-simāṭa fa-akalnā wa-sharibnā ḥattā iktafaynā wa-dakhala ʿalaynā fa-akhadhanī wa-dakhala ilā al-firāshi
sentences.l: So he rejoiced a strong rejoicing and embraced me, and love of him took the gatherings of my heart; and they set before us the spread, and we ate and drank until we were satisfied, and he came in upon us, and took me, and went into the bed.
sentences.i: He was overjoyed and embraced me, and my love for him took hold of every corner of my heart. They laid the table before us and we ate and drank our fill; then he came in to me, took me, and went with me to bed.
sentences.n: مَجَامِعَ قَلْبِي, 'the gathering-places of my heart', means the whole of it. وَدَخَلَ عَلَيْنَا: دَخَلَ عَلَى is the standing phrase for going in to someone, here the bridegroom coming to the bride.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلْ فِي بَوْسٍ وَعِنَاقٍ إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ وَلَمْ يَزَلْ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْحَالَةِ مُدَّةَ شَهْرٍ وَنَحْنُ فِي هَنَأٍ وَسُرُورٍ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazal fī bawsin wa-ʿināqin ilā al-ṣabāḥi wa-lam yazal ʿalā hādhihi al-ḥālati muddata shahrin wa-naḥnu fī hanaʾin wa-surūrin
sentences.l: And he did not cease in kissing and embracing until the morning, and he did not cease in this state for the span of a month, while we were in ease and gladness.
sentences.i: He never stopped kissing and embracing me until morning, and he went on in this way for a whole month, while we lived in comfort and joy.
sentences.n: هَنَأٍ is printed with a hamza after nūn and no alif, for Classical هَنَاءٍ 'ease'; it is pointed as printed.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ الشَّهْرِ اسْتَأْذَنْتُهُ فِي أَنِّي أَسِيرُ إِلَى السُّوقِ وَأَشْتَرِي بَعْضَ قُمَاشٍ فَأَذِنَ لِي فِى الرَّوَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda al-shahri istaʾdhantuhu fī annī asīru ilā al-sūqi wa-ashtarī baʿḍa qumāshin fa-adhina lī fī al-rawāḥi
sentences.l: And after the month I asked his permission that I go to the market and buy some cloth; and he permitted me in the going.
sentences.i: After the month I asked his leave to go to the market and buy some cloth, and he gave me leave to go.

sentences.t: فَتَزَيَّرْتُ وَأَخَذْتُ الْعَجُوزَ مَعِي وَجَارِيَةً وَنَزَلْتُ إِلَى السُّوقِ فَجَلَسْتُ عَلَى دُكَّانِ شَابٍّ تَاجِرٍ تَعْرِفُهُ الْعَجُوزُ
sentences.tr: fa-tazayyartu wa-akhadhtu al-ʿajūza maʿī wa-jāriyatan wa-nazaltu ilā al-sūqi fa-jalastu ʿalā dukkāni shābbin tājirin taʿrifuhu al-ʿajūzu
sentences.l: So I adorned myself, and took the old woman with me and a slave-girl, and went down to the market, and sat at the shop of a youth, a merchant, whom the old woman knew.
sentences.i: I dressed myself finely, took the old woman and a maid with me, and went down to the market. There I sat down at the shop of a young merchant whom the old woman knew.
sentences.n: فَتَزَيَّرْتُ is printed with ر where the sense wants ن, for تَزَيَّنْتُ 'I adorned myself'. It is pointed with the letters printed and read as a slip; this is the same kind of ر/ن slip that turns up in Middle Arabic manuscripts.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لِي هَذَا وَلَدٌ صَغِيرٌ مَاتَ أَبُوهُ وَخَلَّفَ لَهُ مَالًا كَثِيرًا وَعِنْدَهُ مَتْجَرٌ عَظِيمٌ وَمَا طَلَبْتِهِ تَجِدُهُ وَمَا عِنْدَ أَحَدٍ فِي السُّوقِ أَحْسَنُ مِنْ قُمَاشِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lī hādhā waladun ṣaghīrun māta abūhu wa-khallafa lahu mālan kathīran wa-ʿindahu matjarun ʿaẓīmun wa-mā ṭalabtihi tajiduhu wa-mā ʿinda aḥadin fī al-sūqi aḥsanu min qumāshihi
sentences.l: And she said to me: This is a young boy; his father died and left to him much wealth, and with him is a great store, and whatever you seek you will find it, and there is not with anyone in the market better than his cloth.
sentences.i: And she said to me, This is a young lad whose father died and left him great wealth. He keeps a fine warehouse, and whatever you ask for you will find; nobody in the market has better cloth than his.
sentences.n: مَا طَلَبْتِهِ 'whatever you (f.) seek' has a resumptive pronoun ـهُ, an easy Middle Arabic construction. أَحْسَنُ after مَا عِنْدَ أَحَدٍ is read as printed, with the nominative.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لَهُ هَاتِ أَعَزَّ مَا عِنْدَكَ مِنَ الْقُمَاشِ لِهَذِهِ الصَّبِيَّةِ فَقَالَ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً فَشَكَرَتْ فِيهِ الْعَجُوزُ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat lahu hāti aʿazza mā ʿindaka mina al-qumāshi li-hādhihi al-ṣabiyyati fa-qāla samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan fa-shakarat fīhi al-ʿajūzu
sentences.l: Then she said to him: Bring the dearest of what is with you of cloth for this girl. And he said, Hearing and obedience. And the old woman thanked, in him.
sentences.i: Then she said to him, Bring out the choicest cloth you have for this young lady. He answered with hearing and obedience, and the old woman fell to praising him.
sentences.n: سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً is an accusative pair meaning 'I give hearing and obedience', an answer of ready compliance. فَشَكَرَتْ فِيهِ, 'she thanked (praised) in him', means she praised him. The لِـ in لِهَذِهِ الصَّبِيَّةِ marks the person the cloth is for.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ مَا لَنَا حَاجَةٌ بِشُكْرِكِ فِيهِ وَمُرَادُنَا نَأْخُذُ حَاجَتَنَا مِنْهُ وَنَعُودُ إِلَى مَنْزِلِنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qultu mā lanā ḥājatun bi-shukriki fīhi wa-murādunā naʾkhudhu ḥājatanā minhu wa-naʿūdu ilā manzilinā
sentences.l: So I said: We have no need of your thanking in him; our wish is we take our need from him and return to our house.
sentences.i: So I said, We have no use for your praise of him. All we want is to take what we need from him and go home.
sentences.n: مُرَادُنَا نَأْخُذُ has no أَنْ between the noun and the verb: 'our wish (is) we take', which Classical Arabic would join with أَنْ. It is the usual Middle Arabic way of linking two clauses without a conjunction. The لِـ in لَنَا is the possessive 'for us / we have'.

sentences.t: فَأَخْرَجَ لَنَا مَاطَلَبْنَاهُ وَأَخْرَجْنَا لَهُ الدَّرَاهِمَ فَأَبَى أَنْ يَأْخُذَ شَيْئًا وَقَالَ هَذِهِ ضِيَافَتُكُمُ الْيَوْمَ عِنْدِي
sentences.tr: fa-akhraja lanā mātalabnāhu wa-akhrajnā lahu al-darāhima fa-abā an yaʾkhudha shayʾan wa-qāla hādhihi ḍiyāfatukumu al-yawma ʿindī
sentences.l: So he brought out for us what we asked for, and we brought out for him the dirhams, and he refused to take anything and said: This is your hospitality today, with me.
sentences.i: So he brought out what we asked for, and we took out the coins for him, but he refused to take a thing. He said, Today you are my guests.
sentences.n: مَاطَلَبْنَاهُ is printed as one run for مَا طَلَبْنَاهُ. أَبَى أَنْ يَأْخُذَ, 'he refused to take', takes أَنْ with the subjunctive.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْعَجُوزُ إِنْ لَمْ تَأْخُذِ الدَّرَاهِمَ وَإِلَّا أُعْطِيهِ قُمَاشَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-ʿajūzu in lam taʾkhudhi al-darāhima wa-illā uʿṭīhi qumāshahu
