sentences.l: So the old woman said: If you do not take the dirhams, otherwise I give him back his cloth.
sentences.i: Then the old woman said, Either you take the money, or I give him back his cloth.
sentences.n: إِنْ لَمْ ... وَإِلَّا is an odd pairing: 'if you do not take the money, and if not (that), I return his cloth'. The sense is a threat to hand back the goods; read it as 'take the money, or else...'. أُعْطِيهِ قُمَاشَهُ is 'I give him his cloth', that is, 'back'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ لَا آخُذُ مِنْكِ شَيْئًا وَالْجَمِيعُ هَدِيَّةٌ مِنْ عِنْدِي فِي بَوْسَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ فَإِنَّهَا عِنْدِي أَحْسَنُ مِنْ جَمِيعِ مَا فِي دُكَّانِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wa-Allāhi lā ākhudhu minki shayʾan wa-al-jamīʿu hadiyyatun min ʿindī fī bawsatin wāḥidatin fa-innahā ʿindī aḥsanu min jamīʿi mā fī dukkānī
sentences.l: So he said: By God, I will not take anything from you, and the whole is a gift from me, in one kiss; for it, with me, is better than all that is in my shop.
sentences.i: But he said, By God, I will take nothing from you. All of it is a gift from me, for a single kiss, for a kiss is worth more to me than everything in my shop.
sentences.n: فِي بَوْسَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ: فِي here means 'in return for, at the price of'. The وَ in وَاللَّهِ is the oath particle, 'by God'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْعَجُوزُ مَا الَّذِي يُفِيدُكَ مِنَ الْبَوْسَةِ ثُمَّ قَالَتْ يَا بِنْتِي سَمِعْتِ مَا قَالَ هَذَا الشَّابُّ وَمَا يُصِيبُكِ إِذَا أَخَذَ مِنْكِ بَوْسَةً وَتَأْخُذِي مَا تَطْلُبِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-ʿajūzu mā al-ladhī yufīduka mina al-bawsati thumma qālat yā bintī samiʿti mā qāla hādhā al-shābbu wa-mā yuṣībuki idhā akhadha minki bawsatan wa-taʾkhudhī mā taṭlubīhi
sentences.l: So the old woman said: What is it that profits you from the kiss? Then she said: O my daughter, you have heard what this youth said; and what befalls you if he takes a kiss from you, and you take what you seek?
sentences.i: The old woman said to him, What good is a kiss to you? Then she turned to me: My daughter, you have heard what this young man says. What harm will come to you if he takes one kiss, and you take what you want?
sentences.n: تَأْخُذِي and تَطْلُبِيهِ carry -ī without final ن (Classical تَأْخُذِينَ, تَطْلُبِينَهُ). وَتَأْخُذِي continues the question after إِذَا: 'if he takes a kiss ... and you take'.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهَا أَنْتِ مَا تَعْرِفِي أَنِّي حَالِفَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahā anti mā taʿrifī annī ḥālifatun
sentences.l: So I said to her: You, you do not know that I am one-who-has-sworn.
sentences.i: I said to her, Do you not know that I have sworn an oath?
sentences.n: مَا تَعْرِفِي is the Middle Arabic negative present (Classical لَا تَعْرِفِينَ / لَمْ تَعْرِفِي), with -ī for -īna again.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ خَلِّيهِ يَبُوسُكِ وَأَنْتِ سَاكِتَةٌ وَ لَا عَلَيْكِ شَيْءٌ وَتَأْخُذِي هَذِهِ الدَّرَاهِمَ وَلَا زَٰلَتْ تُحَسِّنُ لِي هَذَا الْأَمْرَ حَتَّى أَدْخَلْتُ رَأْسِي الْجِرَابَ وَرَضِيتُ بِذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat khallihi yabūsuki wa-anti sākitatun wa lā ʿalayki shayʾun wa-taʾkhudhī hādhihi al-darāhima wa-lā zālat tuḥassinu lī hādhā al-amra ḥattā adkhaltu raʾsī al-jirāba wa-raḍītu bi-dhālika
sentences.l: So she said: Let him kiss you while you are silent, and nothing is upon you, and you take these dirhams. And she did not cease to make this matter fair to me until I put my head in the bag and was content with that.
sentences.i: She said, Let him kiss you while you keep quiet. No blame falls on you, and you take the coins. And she went on making the thing seem harmless to me until I put my head in the bag, and agreed to it.
sentences.n: وَلَا زَٰلَتْ is printed without the alif of زَالَتْ; the dagger alif supplies it ('she did not cease'). أَدْخَلْتُ رَأْسِي الْجِرَابَ is a saying about putting one's head into the bag, that is, walking into the trap; the sense here is 'I gave in'. The stray وَ before لَا is the edition's line-end spacing, kept. رَضِيتُ بِذَلِكَ: the verb رَضِيَ takes بِـ for what one is content with.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنِّي غَطَّيْتُ عَيْنِي وَدَارَيْتُ بِطَرَفِ إِزَارِي مِنَ النَّاسِ وَحَطَّ فَمَهُ تَحْتَ إِزَارِي عَلَى حَدِّي
sentences.tr: thumma innī ghaṭṭaytu ʿaynī wa-dāraytu bi-ṭarafi izārī mina al-nāsi wa-ḥaṭṭa famahu taḥta izārī ʿalā ḥaddī
sentences.l: Then I covered my eye and screened myself with the edge of my wrap from the people, and he put his mouth under my wrap upon my cheek.
sentences.i: Then I covered my eyes and screened myself from the crowd with the edge of my wrap, and he put his mouth under it, against my cheek.
sentences.n: عَلَى حَدِّي is printed with ح; the following sentence shows that خَدِّي, 'my cheek', is meant. The letters are kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا بَاسَنِى عَضَّنِي عَضَّةً قَوِيَّةً قَطَعَ مِنْ خَدِّي اللَّحْمَةَ فَغُشِيَ عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā bāsanī ʿaḍḍanī ʿaḍḍatan qawiyyatan qaṭaʿa min khaddī al-laḥmata fa-ghushiya ʿalayya
sentences.l: So when he kissed me, he bit me a strong bite; he cut from my cheek the flesh; and I was overcome.
sentences.i: But when he kissed me he bit me hard, tearing the flesh from my cheek, and I fainted.
sentences.n: غُشِيَ عَلَيَّ, 'it was covered upon me', is the ordinary way to say 'I swooned'.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَخَذَتْنِي الْعَجُوزُ فِي حِضْنِهَا فَلَمَّا أَفَقْتُ وَجَدْتُ الدُّكَّانَ مَقْفُولَةً وَالْعَجُوزُ تُظْهِرُ لِي الْحُزْنَ وَتَقُولُ دَفَعَ اللَّهُ مَاكَانَ أَعْظَمَ
sentences.tr: thumma akhadhatnī al-ʿajūzu fī ḥiḍnihā fa-lammā afaqtu wajadtu al-dukkāna maqfūlatan wa-al-ʿajūzu tuẓhiru lī al-ḥuzna wa-taqūlu dafaʿa Allāhu mākāna aʿẓama
sentences.l: Then the old woman took me into her lap; and when I came to, I found the shop locked, and the old woman showing me grief and saying: God has warded off what was greater.
sentences.i: Then the old woman took me in her arms. When I came round I found the shop shut up, and the old woman putting on a show of grief and saying, God be praised, it might have been far worse.
sentences.n: الدُّكَّانَ مَقْفُولَةً treats دُكَّان as feminine ('shut', f.), which Classical does not. دَفَعَ اللَّهُ مَاكَانَ أَعْظَمَ is 'God repelled what would have been greater', a phrase of consolation, 'it could have been worse'. مَاكَانَ is printed as one run.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لِي قُومِي بِنَا إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَشُدِّي رُوحَكِ لِئَلَّا تَنْفَضِحِي
sentences.tr: thumma qālat lī qūmī binā ilā al-bayti wa-shuddī rūḥaki li-iʾallā tanfaḍiḥī
sentences.l: Then she said to me: Arise with us to the house, and brace your soul lest you be disgraced.
sentences.i: Then she said to me, Get up and come home with me, and pull yourself together, or you will be shamed.
sentences.n: رُوحَكِ 'your soul' is the common Middle Arabic reflexive, 'yourself' (here and below). قُومِي بِنَا, 'rise with us', means 'come along'.

sentences.t: فَإِذَا وَصَلْتِ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ ارْقُدِي وَتَضَاعَفِي رُوحَكِ مَرِيضَةً وَارْمِي عَلَيْكِ الْغَطَا وَأَنَا أَجِيءُ لَكِ بِدَوَاءٍ تُدَاوِي بِهِ هَذِهِ الْعَضَّةَ فَتَبْرَىءُ سَرِيعًا
sentences.tr: fa-idhā waṣalti ilā al-bayti irqudī wa-taḍāʿafī rūḥaki marīḍatan wa-irmī ʿalayki al-ghaṭā wa-anā ajīʾu laki bi-dawāʾin tudāwī bihi hādhihi al-ʿaḍḍata fa-tabraʾu sarīʿan
sentences.l: So when you reach the house, lie down, and double yourself, your soul, sick, and cast the cover over you, and I will come to you with a medicine with which you treat this bite, and it will heal quickly.
sentences.i: When you reach the house, lie down, make yourself out to be ill, and draw the coverlet over you. I will bring you a medicine to treat this bite, and it will soon mend.
sentences.n: وَتَضَاعَفِي is obscure. As printed it is the imperative of form VI, which would be 'make yourself double'. It is read here as 'pretend, make yourself out to be' (compare تَمَارَضَ 'feign illness'), but the printing may hide another verb. الْغَطَا is spelled without the final hamza of الْغِطَاءِ. فَتَبْرَىءُ is printed with ى before the hamza; it is read as تَبْرَأُ 'it (the bite) heals', though 'you will recover' (تَبْرَئِينَ) is also possible. بِدَوَاءٍ after أَجِيءُ: جَاءَ بِـ means 'bring'.

sentences.t: فَبَعْدَ سَاعَةٍ قُمْتُ مِنْ مَكَانِي وَأَنَا فِي غَايَةِ الْفِكْرِ وَاشْتَدَّ بِي الْخَوْفُ وَمَشَيْتُ قَلِيلًا قَلِيلًا حَتَّى وَصَلْتُ الْبَيْتَ وَصِرْتُ فِي حَالَةِ الْمَرَضِ
sentences.tr: fa-baʿda sāʿatin qumtu min makānī wa-anā fī ghāyati al-fikri wa-ishtadda bī al-khawfu wa-mashaytu qalīlan qalīlan ḥattā waṣaltu al-bayta wa-ṣirtu fī ḥālati al-maraḍi
sentences.l: So after an hour I rose from my place, while I was in the extreme of thought, and fear grew strong upon me, and I walked little by little until I reached the house, and I became in the state of sickness.
sentences.i: After an hour I got up from my place, in the depths of anxiety, with fear growing on me, and walked slowly, bit by bit, until I reached the house, where I put myself in the posture of an invalid.
sentences.n: اشْتَدَّ بِي الْخَوْفُ: 'fear grew strong with me', where بِـ marks the person who feels it. قَلِيلًا قَلِيلًا, 'little little', means 'slowly, by degrees'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ اللَّيْلُ وَإِذَا بِزَوْجِي دَخَلَ وَقَالَ مَا الَّذِي أَصَابَكِ يَا سَيِّدَتِي فِي هَذِهِ الْخَرْجَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhala al-laylu wa-idhā bi-zawjī dakhala wa-qāla mā al-ladhī aṣābaki yā sayyidatī fī hādhihi al-kharjati
sentences.l: So when the night had entered, and behold, my husband came in and said: What is it that has befallen you, O my lady, on this going-out?
sentences.i: When night fell, behold, my husband came in and said, What has happened to you, my lady, on this outing?
sentences.n: فَلَمَّا ... وَإِذَا بِزَوْجِي: the answer to لَمَّا is introduced by وَإِذَا 'and behold', a Middle Arabic and colloquial style; the بِـ marks the newcomer.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ مَا أَنَا طَيِّبَةٌ وَجَعٌ فِي رَأْسِي فَنَظَرَ إِلَيَّ فَأَوْقَدَ شَمْعَةً وَقَرَّبَ مِنِّي
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu mā anā ṭayyibatun wajaʿun fī raʾsī fa-naẓara ilayya fa-awqada shamʿatan wa-qarraba minnī
sentences.l: So I said to him: I am not well, a pain in my head. And he looked at me, and lit a candle, and drew near to me.
sentences.i: I said to him, I am not well: I have a pain in my head. He looked at me, lit a candle, and came close to me.
sentences.n: مَا أَنَا طَيِّبَةٌ: 'I am not well', with مَا before a pronoun and predicate, colloquial rather than Classical. وَجَعٌ فِي رَأْسِي is a bare noun phrase, 'a pain in my head'.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ مَا هَذَا الْجُرْحُ الَّذِي فِي خَدِّكِ وَهُوَ فِى الْمَكَانِ النَّاعِمِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla mā hādhā al-jurḥu al-ladhī fī khaddiki wa-huwa fī al-makāni al-nāʿimi
sentences.l: And he said: What is this wound that is in your cheek, and it is in the soft place?
sentences.i: And he said, What is this wound on your cheek, and on the softest part of it, too?

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ إِنِّي لَمَّا اسْتَأْذَنْتُكَ وَخَرَجْتُ فِي هَذَا النَّهَارِ أَشْتَرِي الْقُمَاشَ زَاحَمَنِي جَمَلُ حَطَبٍ فَشَرْمَطَ نِقَابِي وَجَرَحَ خَدِّي كَمَاتَرَى فَإِنَّ الْمَكَانَ ضَيِّقٌ فِي هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu innī lammā istaʾdhantuka wa-kharajtu fī hādhā al-nahāri ashtarī al-qumāsha zāḥamanī jamalu ḥaṭabin fa-sharmaṭa niqābī wa-jaraḥa khaddī kamātarā fa-inna al-makāna ḍayyiqun fī hādhihi al-madīnati
sentences.l: So I said: When I asked your leave and went out on this day to buy the cloth, a camel of firewood jostled me, and it tore my veil to shreds and wounded my cheek, as you see; for the place is narrow in this city.
sentences.i: I said, When I asked your leave and went out today to buy cloth, a camel laden with firewood jostled me, shredded my veil and gashed my cheek, as you see; the streets of this city are so cramped.
sentences.n: جَمَلُ حَطَبٍ 'a camel of firewood' is a camel loaded with wood. أَشْتَرِي الْقُمَاشَ, 'I buy the cloth', gives the purpose without any particle. كَمَاتَرَى is printed as one run (كَمَا تَرَى) 'as you see'. The wound claimed here is the lie that begins a small cycle of false excuses.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ غَدًا أَرُوحُ لِلْحَاكِمِ وَأَقُولُ لَهُ يَشْنُقُ كُلَّ حَطَّابٍ فِى الْمَدِينَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ghadan arūḥu li-al-ḥākimi wa-aqūlu lahu yashnuqu kulla ḥaṭṭābin fī al-madīnati
sentences.l: So he said: Tomorrow I go to the ruler, and I say to him, He hangs every wood-cutter in the city.
sentences.i: He said, Tomorrow I will go to the governor and tell him to hang every woodcutter in the city.
sentences.n: أَرُوحُ لِلْحَاكِمِ: لِـ here means 'to' (towards) the governor. يَشْنُقُ carries no أَنْ: 'I say to him: let him hang', a bare present standing for a command.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ لَا تَحْتَمِلْ خَطِيئَةَ أَحَدٍ فَإِنِّي رَكِبْتُ حِمَارًا فَعَثَرَ بِي فَنَزَلْتُ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ فَصَادَفَنِي عُودٌ خَدَشَ خَدِّي وَ جَرَحَنِي
sentences.tr: fa-qultu bi-Allāhi ʿalayka lā taḥtamil khaṭīʾata aḥadin fa-innī rakibtu ḥimāran fa-ʿathara bī fa-nazaltu ʿalā al-arḍi fa-ṣādafanī ʿūdun khadasha khaddī wa jaraḥanī
sentences.l: So I said: By God upon you, do not bear the sin of anyone; for I rode a donkey, and it stumbled with me, and I came down onto the ground, and a stick met me and scratched my cheek and wounded me.
sentences.i: I said, For God's sake, do not take anyone's guilt upon you; for the truth is that I rode a donkey and it stumbled under me, and I fell to the ground and a stick caught me and scratched and cut my cheek.
sentences.n: بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ is an entreaty: بِـ is the oath-preposition, 'by God (I beg) you'. فَعَثَرَ بِي, 'it stumbled with me', means it stumbled while I was riding. Note the contradiction with her first story: she now blames a donkey, not a camel of firewood.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ غَدًا أَطْلَعُ لِجَعْفَرٍ الْبَرْمَكِيِّ وَأَحْكِي لَهُ الْحِكَايَةَ فَيَقْتُلُ كُلَّ حِمَارٍ فِي هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ghadan aṭlaʿu li-Jaʿfarin al-Barmakiyyi wa-aḥkī lahu al-ḥikāyata fa-yaqtulu kulla ḥimārin fī hādhihi al-madīnati
sentences.l: So he said: Tomorrow I go up to Jaʿfar the Barmakid and tell him the tale, and he kills every donkey in this city.
sentences.i: He said, Tomorrow I will go up to Jaʿfar the Barmakid and tell him the story, and he will have every donkey in this city killed.
sentences.n: لِجَعْفَرٍ: لِـ after أَطْلَعُ marks the person one goes up to. جَعْفَر الْبَرْمَكِي is the vizier of Hārūn al-Rashīd, and so of the caliph to whom the woman is telling her story.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ أَنْتَ تُضِيعُ النَّاسَ كُلَّهُمْ بِسَبَبِي وَ هَذَا الَّذِي جَرَى لِى بِقَضَاءِ اللَّهِ وَقَدَرِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu anta tuḍīʿu al-nāsa kullahum bi-sababī wa hādhā al-ladhī jarā lī bi-qaḍāʾi Allāhi wa-qadarihi
sentences.l: So I said: You ruin all the people because of me, and this that has happened to me is by the decree of God and His ordaining.
sentences.i: I said, Will you ruin everybody on my account? What has happened to me came by the decree of God and his ordaining.
sentences.n: بِسَبَبِي 'because of me' uses بِـ for cause; بِقَضَاءِ اللَّهِ uses it for the means, 'by' God's decree. The stray وَ before هَذَا is the edition's line-end spacing, kept.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَابُدَّ مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَلَحَّ عَلَيَّ بِالْكَلَامِ وَنَهَضَ قَائِمًا فَنَفَرْتُ مِنْهُ وَأَغْلَظْتُ كَلَامِي عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lābudda min dhālika wa-laḥḥa ʿalayya bi-al-kalāmi wa-nahaḍa qāʾiman fa-nafartu minhu wa-aghlaẓtu kalāmī ʿalayhi
sentences.l: So he said: There is no escape from that; and he pressed upon me with talk, and rose up standing, and I shied from him and made my speech coarse upon him.
sentences.i: He said, It must be done. He pressed me hard with his words and sprang to his feet, and I shrank from him and answered him roughly.
sentences.n: لَابُدَّ مِنْ ذَلِكَ, 'no escape from that', means 'it must be so'; لَابُدَّ is printed as one run. لَحَّ عَلَيَّ بِالْكَلَامِ: the verb takes بِـ for what it presses with.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلِمَ بِحَالِى وَقَالَ خُنْتِى الْيَمِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika yā amīra al-muʾminīna ʿalima bi-ḥālī wa-qāla khuntī al-yamīna
sentences.l: So at that, O commander of the believers, he knew of my state and said: You have broken the oath.
sentences.i: At that, Commander of the Faithful, he understood my condition and said, You have broken your oath.
sentences.n: خُنْتِى is printed with ى for the final long -ī; it is read as خُنْتِ 'you (f.) have betrayed', with the ى left as printed. عَلِمَ بِحَالِي, 'he knew of my state', takes بِـ for the thing learned. Here the narrator turns aside to address the caliph.

sentences.t: وَصَاحَ صَيْحَةً عَظِيمَةً فَانْفَتَحَ الْبَابُ وَطَلَعَ مِنْهُ سَبْعُ عَبِيدٍ سُودٍ وَأَمَرَهُمْ فَسَحَبُونِي مِنْ فِرْشِي وَرَمَوْنِي وَسَطَ الدَّارِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāḥa ṣayḥatan ʿaẓīmatan fa-infataḥa al-bābu wa-ṭalaʿa minhu sabʿu ʿabīdin sūdin wa-amarahum fa-saḥabūnī min firshī wa-ramawnī wasaṭa al-dāri
sentences.l: And he cried a great cry, and the door opened, and there came out of it seven slaves, black-ones, and he commanded them, and they dragged me from my bedding and threw me in the middle of the house.
sentences.i: He gave a great shout, and the door opened and seven black slaves came out. He gave them their orders, and they dragged me from my bedding and flung me down in the middle of the house.
sentences.n: سَبْعُ عَبِيدٍ سُودٍ has سَبْع without ة before a masculine plural, and a plural adjective: Middle Arabic, kept as printed. وَأَمَرَهُمْ فَسَحَبُونِي, 'and he commanded them, so they dragged', gives the order and the deed without a أَنْ clause.

sentences.t: وَأَمَرَ عَبْدًا مِنْهُمْ أَنْ يُمْسِكَنِي مِنْ أَكْتَافِي وَيَجْلِسَ عَلَى رَأْسِي وَأَمَرَ الثَّانِيَ أَنْ يَجْلِسَ عَلَى رُكْبَتَيَّ وَيُمْسِكَ رِجْلَيَّ
sentences.tr: wa-amara ʿabdan minhum an yumsikanī min aktāfī wa-yajlisa ʿalā raʾsī wa-amara al-thāniya an yajlisa ʿalā rukbatayya wa-yumsika rijlayya
sentences.l: And he commanded a slave of them to hold me by my shoulders and to sit upon my head, and he commanded the second to sit upon my knees and to hold my legs.
sentences.i: He ordered one of them to hold me by the shoulders and sit on my head, and told the second to sit on my knees and pin my legs.
sentences.n: رُكْبَتَيَّ and رِجْلَيَّ are read as duals ('my two knees', 'my two legs'), which the unmarked printing allows. أَمَرَهُ أَنْ ...: أَمَرَ takes the object and a أَنْ clause for what is commanded.

sentences.t: وَجَاءَ الثَّالِثُ وَفِي يَدِهِ سَيْفٌ فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا سَيِّدِي اضْرِبْهَا بِالسَّيْفِ اقْسِمْهَا نِصْفَيْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-jāʾa al-thālithu wa-fī yadihi sayfun fa-qāla lahu yā sayyidī iḍribhā bi-al-sayfi iqsimhā niṣfayni
sentences.l: And the third came, and in his hand a sword, and he said to him: O my master, strike her with the sword, divide her into two halves,
sentences.i: The third came with a sword in his hand and said to him, Master, strike her with the sword and cut her in two,

sentences.t: وَكُلُّ وَاحِدٍ يَأْخُذُ قِطْعَةً يَرْمِيهَا فِي بَحْرِ الدِّجْلَةِ يَأْكُلُهَا السَّمَكُ
sentences.tr: wa-kullu wāḥidin yaʾkhudhu qiṭʿatan yarmīhā fī baḥri al-Dijlati yaʾkuluhā al-samaku
sentences.l: And each one takes a piece, throws it into the sea of the Tigris; the fish eat it.
sentences.i: and let each of us take a piece and throw it in the Tigris for the fish to eat.
sentences.n: The three verbs يَأْخُذُ, يَرْمِيهَا, يَأْكُلُهَا follow one another with no connecting word, so the slave's plan is read as a run of purposes: 'takes a piece, throws it, (for) the fish (to) eat it'. بَحْر is any wide water; here the river Tigris (دِجْلَة, printed with الـ).

sentences.t: وَهَذَا جَزَاءُ مَنْ يَخُونُ الْأَيْمَانَ وَالْمَوَدَّةَ
sentences.tr: wa-hādhā jazāʾu man yakhūnu al-aymāna wa-al-mawaddata
sentences.l: And this is the recompense of whoever betrays the oaths and the affection.
sentences.i: This is the reward of one who betrays her oaths and the love she is owed.
sentences.n: الْأَيْمَانَ is read as the plural of يَمِين 'oaths', which fits خُنْتِي الْيَمِينَ above; الْإِيمَانَ 'faith' is the other possible reading of the bare letters.

sentences.t: وَاشْتَدَّ غَضَبُهُ وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: wa-ishtadda ghaḍabuhu wa-anshada yaqūlu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: And his anger grew strong, and he recited, saying these verses:
sentences.i: His anger grew hotter still, and he recited these lines:

sentences.t:
إِنْ كَانَ لِي فِيمَنْ أُحِبُّ مُشَارِكًا * مَنَعْتُ الْهَوَى رُوحِي وَلَوْا تَلَفَهُ وَجْدِي
وَقُلْتُ لَهَا يَا نَفْسُ مُوتِي كَرِيمَةً * فَلَا خَيْرَ فِي حُبٍّ يَكُونُ عَلَى ضِدٍّ
sentences.tr:
in kāna lī fīman uḥibbu mushārikan * manaʿtu al-hawā rūḥī wa-law-ā talafahu wajdī
wa-qultu lahā yā nafsu mūtī karīmatan * fa-lā khayra fī ḥubbin yakūnu ʿalā ḍiddin
sentences.l:
If there be to me, in the one I love, a sharer * I have forbidden love to my soul, even-if my longing ruin it,
And I said to her: O soul, die noble * for there is no good in a love that is against an opposite.
sentences.i: If I must share the one I love, then I forbid my soul love, though longing should waste it away; and I said to it, 'O soul, die nobly, for there is no good in a love that is that has a rival.'
sentences.n: The archive prints ولوا تلفه with the alif on the wrong word; the sense is وَلَوْ أَتْلَفَهُ 'even if it destroyed it'. The words are kept as printed, with the first vocalised as وَلَوْا and the second as تَلَفَهُ, so read them together as 'even if my longing destroyed it'. ضِدٍّ 'an opposite, a rival' is the last word of the couplet, and the line seems to say that a love that shares its object is a love working against itself.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَٰلَ لِلْعَبْدِ أَخْبِرْنَا يَا سَعْدُ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla li-al-ʿabdi akhbirnā yā Saʿdu
sentences.l: Then he said to the slave: 'Inform us, O Saʿd.'
sentences.i: Then he said to the slave, 'Tell us, Saʿd.'
sentences.n: The young man is speaking, and he addresses his slave, Saʿd.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا تَحَقَّقَ الْعَبْدُ جَلَسَ عَلَيَّ وَقَالَ يَا سَيِّدَتِي اذْكُرِي الشَّهَادَةَ وَمَاكَانَ لَكِ مِنَ الْحَوَائِجِ أَخْبِرِينَابِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā taḥaqqaqa al-ʿabdu jalasa ʿalayya wa-qāla yā sayyidatī udhkurī al-shahādata wa-mākāna laki mina al-ḥawāʾiji akhbirīnābihi
sentences.l: So when the slave was certain, he sat upon me and said: O my lady, mention the testimony, and what there was for you of needs, inform-us-of-it,
sentences.i: When the slave was satisfied of it, he sat down upon me and said, 'My lady, pronounce the profession of faith, and tell us of any wants you have,
sentences.n: Two pairs of words are printed run together, and both are read as two words without changing a letter: وَمَاكَانَ is وَمَا كَانَ 'and what there was', and أَخْبِرِينَابِهِ is أَخْبِرِينَا بِهِ 'tell us of it'. اذْكُرِي الشَّهَادَةَ, 'mention the testimony', means to say the Muslim profession of faith before death. The clause continues into the next unit.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ هَذَا آخِرُ حَيَوٰتِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-inna hādhā ākhiru ḥayātiki
sentences.l: for indeed this is the last of your life.
sentences.i: for this is the last of your life.'
sentences.n: حَيَوٰتِكِ is printed حيوتك for حياتك, the same way صلوة is sometimes written for صلاة; the dagger alif on the wāw shows the vowel. Read it ḥayātiki.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ يَا عَبْدَ الْخَيْرِ تَمَهَّلْ عَلَيَّ قَلِيلًا حَتَّى أُوصِيَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu yā ʿabda al-khayri tamahhal ʿalayya qalīlan ḥattā ūṣiyaka
sentences.l: So I said to him: O slave-of-the-good, take-your-time upon me a little, until I charge you.
sentences.i: So I said to him, 'Good slave, give me a little time, until I lay my charge upon you.'
sentences.n: يَا عَبْدَ الْخَيْرِ is a polite form of address, 'servant of goodness', here half-ironic. أُوصِيَكَ is the subjunctive after حَتَّى 'until', and وَصَّى / أَوْصَى 'to charge, to leave a last request' is what a dying person does.

sentences.t: فَرَفَعْتُ رَأْسِي وَنَظَرْتُ إِلَى حَالِي وَكَيْفَ صِرْتُ فِي الذُّلِّ بَعْدَ الْعِزِّ فَجَرَتْ عَبْرَتِي وَبَكَيْتُ بُكَاءًا شَدِيدًا
sentences.tr: fa-rafaʿtu raʾsī wa-naẓartu ilā ḥālī wa-kayfa ṣirtu fī al-dhulli baʿda al-ʿizzi fa-jarat ʿabratī wa-bakaytu bukāʾan shadīdan
sentences.l: So I raised my head and looked at my condition, and how I had become in the abasement after the might, and my tear ran, and I wept a violent weeping,
sentences.i: I raised my head and looked upon my state, and how I had fallen into abasement from honour; my tears ran down, and I wept bitterly,
sentences.n: بُكَاءًا is printed with a final alif after the hamza, which the edition writes for the accusative ending; it is read bukāʾan, 'a weeping', as a cognate object of بَكَيْتُ.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَ إِلَيَّ بِعَيْنِ الْغَضَبِ وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓara ilayya bi-ʿayni al-ghaḍabi wa-anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: and he looked at me with the eye of anger, and recited, saying:
sentences.i: and he looked at me with an eye of anger, and recited:

sentences.t:
قُلْ لِمَنْ مَلَّ وَصْلَنَا وَجَفَانَا * وَارْتَضَى فِي الْهَوَى خَلِيلًا سِوَانَا
بْٔسُنَا مِنْكَ قَبْلَ بْٔسِكَ مِنَّا * الَّذِي كَانَ بَيْنَنَا قَدْ كَفَانَا
sentences.tr:
qul li-man malla waṣlanā wa-jafānā * wa-irtaḍā fī al-hawā khalīlan siwānā
baʾsunā minka qabla baʾsika minnā * alladhī kāna baynanā qad kafānā
sentences.l:
Say to him who wearied of our joining and shunned us * and was content, in love, with a friend other than us:
Our distress from you, before your distress from us * what was between us has already sufficed us.
sentences.i: Say to him who grew weary of our company, who shunned us and settled in love upon another friend: our distress over you came before your distress over us; what lay between us is enough for us.
sentences.n: The printed words بسنا and بسك are obscure, and the archive gives no vowel or hamza. They are read here as بَْٔسُنَا 'our distress' and بَْٔسِكَ 'your distress', from the root بأس 'distress, hardship', which gives a tolerable sense ('our distress over you came before yours over us'). The word may instead be a slip for يَئِسْنَا 'we despaired' and يَأْسِكَ 'your despair', which would give 'we despaired of you before you despaired of us'; take the reading with caution.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُهُ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بَكَيْتُ وَنَظَرْتُ إِلَيْهِ وَأَنْشَدْتُ أَقُولُ هَذِةِ الْأَبْيَاتَ شِعْرٌ —
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtuhu yā amīra al-muʾminīna bakaytu wa-naẓartu ilayhi wa-anshadtu aqūlu hādhihi al-abyāta shiʿrun —
sentences.l: So when I heard him, O commander of the believers, I wept, and looked at him, and recited, saying these verses: verse —
sentences.i: When I heard him, Commander of the Faithful, I wept and looked at him, and I recited these verses:
sentences.n: هَذِةِ is printed هذة, with ة for the usual ه, and is read hādhihi. The stray word شِعْرٌ 'poetry' after the verses is a kind of label, left as printed, and the dash marks that the verses follow.

sentences.t:
أَقَمْتُمْ فِرَاقِي فِي الْهَوَى وَقَعَدْتُمْ * وَأَسْهَرْتُمْ جَفْنِي الْقَرِيحَ وَنِمْتُمْ
وَأَلْفَيْتُمْ بَيْنَ السُّهَادِ وَنَاظِرِي * فَلَا الْقَلْبُ يَسْلَاكُمْ وَلَا الدَّمْعُ يَكْتُمُ
وَعَاهَدْتُمُونِي أَنَّكُمْ تُحْسِنُوا الْوَفَا * فَلَمَّا تَمَلَّكْتُمْ فُؤَادِي غَدَرْتُمْ
عَشِقْتُكُمْ طِفْلًا فَلَمْ أَدْرِ مَا الْهَوَى * فَلَا تَقْتُلُونِي إِنَّنِي مُتَعَلِّمُ
سَأَلْتُكُمُوا بِاللَّهِ إِنْ مُتُّ فَاكْتُبُوا * عَلَى لَوْحِ قَبْرِي إِنَّ هَذَا مُتَيَّمُ
لَعَلَّ شَجِيًّا عَارِفًا لَوْعَةَ الْهَوَى * يَمُرُّ عَلَى قَلْبِ الْمُحِبِّ فَيَرْحَمُ
sentences.tr:
aqamtum firāqī fī al-hawā wa-qaʿadtum * wa-asharhtum jafnī al-qarīḥa wa-nimtum
wa-alfaytum bayna al-suhādi wa-nāẓirī * fa-lā al-qalbu yaslākum wa-lā al-damʿu yaktumu
wa-ʿāhadtumūnī annakum tuḥsinū al-wafā * fa-lammā tamallaktum fuʾādī ghadartum
ʿashiqtukum ṭiflan fa-lam adri mā al-hawā * fa-lā taqtulūnī innanī mutaʿallimu
saʾaltukumū bi-allāhi in muttu fa-uktubū * ʿalā lawḥi qabrī inna hādhā mutayyamu
laʿalla shajiyyan ʿārifan lawʿata al-hawā * yamurru ʿalā qalbi al-muḥibbi fa-yarḥamu
sentences.l:
You raised-up my parting in love, and you sat * and you kept my sore eyelid wakeful, and you slept,
And you found [me] between the sleeplessness and my eye * so the heart does not forget you, nor does the tear conceal.
And you made a covenant with me that you would do good the faith * then when you had taken-possession of my heart, you betrayed.
I loved you as a child and did not know what love is * so do not kill me; I am a learner.
I ask you by God: if I die, then write * upon the tablet of my grave: 'This one was love-enslaved,'
Perhaps a sorrowful one, knowing the anguish of love * will pass by the heart of the lover, and have mercy.
sentences.i: You brought about my parting in love and then sat idle; you kept my sore eyelid wakeful and slept yourselves. You left me between sleeplessness and my own eyes, so that my heart cannot forget you, nor my tears keep the secret. You swore to me that you would keep faith well, and once you had taken possession of my heart, you betrayed it. I loved you as a child, not knowing what love is; do not kill me, I am still a learner. I beg you by God: if I die, write upon my gravestone, 'This one was love-enslaved,' that perhaps some sorrowing soul who knows the anguish of love will pass by the lover's heart and take pity.
sentences.n: The first two lines are hard, and the wording of the first, أَقَمْتُمْ فِرَاقِي, is taken loosely: 'you set my parting going' while you stayed seated. In the second line أَلْفَيْتُمْ is read 'you found' (or 'left') and the sense is a guess. تُحْسِنُوا has lost its final nūn after أَنَّ, where Classical Arabic requires تُحْسِنُونَ, and سَأَلْتُكُمُوا keeps an old -kumū plural ending; both are printed so and are pointed as printed. In line four the printed rhyme word is مُتَعَلِّمُ, read with the rhyme-vowel damma.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغْتُ مِنْ شِعْرِي بَكَيْتُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghtu min shiʿrī bakaytu
sentences.l: So when I had finished from my verse, I wept.
sentences.i: When I had finished my verses I wept.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الشِّعْرَ وَنَظَرَ إِلَى بُكَائِي ازْدَادَ غَيْظًا عَلَى غَيْظِهِ وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ —
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-shiʿra wa-naẓara ilā bukāʾī izdāda ghayẓan ʿalā ghayẓihi wa-anshada yaqūlu —
sentences.l: So when he heard the verse and looked at my weeping, he increased in rage upon his rage, and recited, saying —
sentences.i: When he heard the poem and saw my tears, his rage grew hotter still, and he recited:

sentences.t:
تَرَكْتُ حَبِيبَ الْقَلْبِ لَا عَنْ مَلَالَةٍ * وَلَكِنْ جَنَى ذَنْبًا يُؤَدِّي إِلَى التَّرْكِ
أَرَادَ شَرِيكًا فِى الْمَحَبَّةِ بَيْنَنَا * وَإِيمَانُ قَلْبِي لَا يَمِيلُ إِلَى الشِّرْكِ
sentences.tr:
taraktu ḥabība al-qalbi lā ʿan malālatin * wa-lākin janā dhanban yuʾaddī ilā al-tarki
arāda sharīkan fī al-maḥabbati baynanā * wa-īmānu qalbī lā yamīlu ilā al-shirki
sentences.l:
I left the beloved of the heart, not from weariness * but he committed a fault that leads to the leaving:
He wanted a partner in love between us * and the faith of my heart does not incline to the associating.
sentences.i: I left the beloved of my heart, not out of weariness, but because he committed a fault that leads to leaving: he wanted a partner in love between us, and the faith of my heart does not lean toward setting up partners.
sentences.n: الشِّرْكِ means 'associating partners with God', the standard term for polytheism, so the last line plays on it: the lover's 'faith' will not allow a partner in love, as faith will not allow one beside God.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ شِعْرِةِ بَكَيْتُ وَتَضَرَّعْتُ لَهُ وَقُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي اخْدَعِيهِ بِالْكَلَامِ لَعَلَّهُ يُعْتِقُنِي مِنَ الْقَتْلِ وَلَوْ كَانَ يَأْخُذُ جَمِيعَ مَا أَمْلِكُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha min shiʿrihi bakaytu wa-taḍarraʿtu lahu wa-qultu fī nafsī ikhdaʿīhi bi-al-kalāmi laʿallahu yuʿtiqunī mina al-qatli wa-law kāna yaʾkhudhu jamīʿa mā amluku
sentences.l: So when he had finished from his verse, I wept and humbled myself to him, and I said in myself: deceive him with speech, perhaps he will free me from the killing, even if he were to take everything that I own.
sentences.i: When he had finished his verses I wept and pleaded with him, and I said to myself, 'Beguile him with words; perhaps he will spare me from being killed, even if he takes everything I own.'
sentences.n: شِعْرِةِ is printed with ة for the pronoun ـه, and is read shiʿrihi 'his poem'. اخْدَعِيهِ is feminine: the speaker is addressing herself.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ شَكَوْتُ إِلَيْهِ مَا أَجِدُهُ وَأَنْشَدْتُ أَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: thumma shakawtu ilayhi mā ajiduhu wa-anshadtu aqūlu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: Then I complained to him of what I was finding, and recited, saying these verses:
sentences.i: Then I told him of all that I was suffering, and recited these verses:

sentences.t:
وَحَقِّكَ لَوْ أَنْصَفْتَنِي مَا قَتَلْتَنِي * وَلَكِنْ حُكْمُ الْبَيْنِ مَا فِيهِ مُنْصِفُ
وَحَمَّلْتَنِي ثِقْلَ الْغَرَامِ وَإِنَّنِي * لَأَعْجَزُ عَنْ حَمْلِ الْقَمِيصِ وَأَضْعَفُ
وَمَا عَجَبِي إِتْلَافُ رُوحِي وَإِنَّمَا * عَجِبْتُ لِجِسْمِي بَعْدَكُمْ كَيْفَ يُعْرَفُ
sentences.tr:
wa-ḥaqqika law anṣaftanī mā qataltanī * wa-lākin ḥukmu al-bayni mā fīhi munṣifu
wa-ḥammaltanī thiqla al-gharāmi wa-innanī * la-aʿjazu ʿan ḥamli al-qamīṣi wa-aḍʿafu
wa-mā ʿajabī itlāfu rūḥī wa-innamā * ʿajibtu li-jismī baʿdakum kayfa yuʿrafu
sentences.i: By your right, if you had dealt fairly with me you would not have killed me; but the rule of parting has no fairness in it. You loaded me with the weight of passion, and I am too helpless even to carry a shirt, and weaker still. It is not the ruin of my soul that astonishes me; I marvel at my body, with you gone, that anyone can still recognise it.
sentences.n: وَحَقِّكَ is an oath, 'by your right' or 'by your truth'. In the second line لَأَعْجَزُ is an emphatic لـ (la-) on the verb after إِنَّ, 'I am indeed more helpless'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغْتُ مِنْ شِعْرِي بَكَيْتُ فَنَظَرَنِي وَنَهَرَنِي وَشَتَمَنِي وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghtu min shiʿrī bakaytu fa-naẓaranī wa-naharanī wa-shatamanī wa-anshada yaqūlu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: So when I had finished from my verse, I wept; and he looked at me and rebuked me and abused me and recited, saying these verses:
sentences.i: When I had finished my verses I wept; and he glared at me, rebuked me and cursed me, and recited these verses:
sentences.n: نَظَرَنِي is printed with a direct object, 'he looked me', where Classical Arabic would say نَظَرَ إِلَيَّ 'he looked at me'; it is read as printed.

sentences.t:
تَشَاغَلْتُمْ عَنَّا بِصُحْبَةِ غَيْرِنَا * وَأَظْهَرْتُمُ الْهِجْرَانَ مَا هَكَذَا كُنَّا
سَأَتْرُكُمْ مِنْ حَيْثُ مَا قَدْ تَرَكْتُمُوا * وَنَصْبِرُ عَنْكُمْ حَقَّ صَبْرِكُمْ عَنَّا
وَنَشْغَلُ عَنْكُمْ مُذْ شُغِلْتُمْ بِغَيْرِنَا * وَنَجْعَلُ قَطْعَ الْوَصْلِ مِنْكُمْ وَلَا مِنَّا
sentences.tr:
tashāghaltum ʿannā bi-ṣuḥbati ghayrinā * wa-aẓhartumu al-hijrāna mā hākadhā kunnā
sa-atrukum min ḥaythu mā qad taraktumū * wa-naṣbiru ʿankum ḥaqqa ṣabrikum ʿannā
wa-nashghalu ʿankum mundhu shughiltum bi-ghayrinā * wa-najʿalu qaṭʿa al-waṣli minkum wa-lā minnā
sentences.l:
You busied yourselves away from us with the company of others than us * and you showed the desertion; not thus were we.
I shall leave you from where you left * and we shall be patient away from you as the due of your patience away from us.
And we shall be occupied away from you since you were occupied with others than us * and we shall make the cutting-off of union be from you, and not from us.
sentences.i: You busied yourselves with other company than ours and showed open desertion; that was not how we were. So I will leave you where you left us, and bear your absence as truly as you bore ours. We will busy ourselves elsewhere, now that you are busy with others, and lay the breaking of the bond at your door, not ours.
sentences.n: These three lines are the young man's parting verses, spoken before he orders the girl killed. They arrive unpointed, so the vowels are ours. سَأَتْرُكُمْ is printed with one ك where 'I shall leave you' (atrukukum) would need two; it is read as printed. The poem shifts from 'I' (سَأَتْرُكُمْ) to 'we' (وَنَصْبِرُ), which is common in verse. مُذْ شُغِلْتُمْ is 'since you were occupied' (passive, with بِـ 'with, by' for the thing that occupied them).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ شِعْرِهِ صَرَخَ عَلَى الْعَبْدِ وَقَالَ لَهُ وَسِّطْهَا وَرَيِّحْنَا مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha min shiʿrihi ṣarakha ʿalā al-ʿabdi wa-qāla lahu wassiṭhā wa-rayyiḥnā minhā
sentences.l: So when he had finished from his verse, he cried out at the slave and said to him: 'Middle her, and give-us-rest from her,
sentences.i: When he had finished his verses, he shouted at the slave and said, 'Cut her in two, and rid us of her,
sentences.n: وَسِّطْهَا is 'cut her through the middle' (from وَسَط 'middle'), the Nights' stock verb for cutting a person in half. The young man's speech runs on into the next unit.

sentences.t: فَلَيْسَ لَنَا فِيهَا فَائِدَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-laysa lanā fīhā fāʾidatun
sentences.l: for there is not for us in her any benefit.'
sentences.i: for she is of no use to us.'

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا نَحْنُ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ نَتَشَاجَرُ بِالْأَشْعَارِ وَقَدْ تَحَقَّقْتُ بِالْمَوْتِ وَأَيِسْتُ مِنَ الْحَيَوٰةِ وَسَلَّمْتُ أَمْرِي لِلَّهِ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā naḥnu yā amīra al-muʾminīna natashājaru bi-al-ashʿāri wa-qad taḥaqqaqtu bi-al-mawti wa-ayistu mina al-ḥayāti wa-sallamtu amrī li-Allāhi taʿālā
sentences.l: So while we, O commander of the believers, were quarrelling with verses, and I had become certain of death and had despaired of life and had handed over my affair to God, exalted is He,
sentences.i: And while we went on wrangling in verse, O Commander of the Faithful, I certain of death, despairing of life, and having given my affair over to God Most High,
sentences.n: بَيْنَمَا 'while' opens a clause that is finished by وَإِذَا 'and suddenly' in the next unit. تَحَقَّقَ بِـ 'be sure of' takes بِـ with the thing known. The narrator is the beaten woman speaking to the caliph.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِالْعَجُوزِ دَخَلَتْ وَرَمَتْ نَفْسَهَا عَلَى أَقْدَامِ الشَّابِّ وَبَاسَتْهُمْ وَ بَكَتْ وَقَالَتْ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-al-ʿajūzi dakhalat wa-ramat nafsahā ʿalā aqdāmi al-shābbi wa-bāsathum wa-bakat wa-qālat
sentences.l: And behold, with the old woman: she entered, and threw herself upon the feet of the young man, and kissed them, and wept, and said:
sentences.i: Then in came the old woman, who threw herself at the young man's feet, kissed them, wept, and said:
sentences.n: وَإِذَا بِ ... is the 'and suddenly' construction: the بِـ only marks what appears. بَاسَتْهُمْ has the masculine-plural -hum for 'the feet', where Classical Arabic would have -hā; a Middle Arabic looseness, kept as printed.

sentences.t: يَا وَلَدِي بِحَقِّ تَرْبِيَتِي لَكَ وَخِدْمَتِي تَعْفُو عَنْ هَٰذِهِ الصَّبِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: yā waladī bi-ḥaqqi tarbiyatī laka wa-khidmatī taʿfū ʿan hādhihi al-ṣabiyyati
sentences.l: 'O my child, by the right of my rearing of you and my service, you pardon concerning this girl,
sentences.i: 'My son, by the claim of my having raised you and served you, forgive this girl,
sentences.n: تَعْفُو is a plain imperfect used as a request ('you will pardon'); Classical Arabic would use the imperative اِعْفُ. It is kept as printed. بِحَقِّ 'by the right of' is an appeal that works like an oath.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّهَا مَا فَعَلَتْ ذَنْبًا يُوجِبُ ذَٰلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-innahā mā faʿalat dhanban yūjibu dhālika
sentences.l: for she has not done a sin that necessitates that,
sentences.i: for she has done nothing that deserves this,

sentences.t: وَأَنْتَ شَابٌّ صَغِيرٌ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ تَدْخُلَ فِي إِثْمِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-anta shābbun ṣaghīrun akhāfu ʿalayka an tadkhula fī ithmihā
sentences.l: and you are a young man, small; I fear for you that you enter into her sin.
sentences.i: You are a young man still, and I fear for you lest you be drawn into the guilt that comes of it.
sentences.n: إِثْمِهَا is 'her sin' or 'the guilt attaching to her': the blood-guilt of killing her. The sense is that she has done no wrong, and the guilt would be his.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ قِيلَ كُلُّ قَاتِلٍ مَقْتُولٌ
sentences.tr: wa-qad qīla kullu qātilin maqtūlun
sentences.l: And it has been said: every killer is killed.
sentences.i: And it has been said, 'Every slayer is slain.'

sentences.t: وَأَيْشِ هَٰذِهِ الْوَسِخَةُ اتْرُكْهَا عَنْكَ وَعَنْ بَالِكَ وَقَلْبِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-ayshi hādhihi al-wasikhatu utrukhā ʿanka wa-ʿan bālika wa-qalbika
sentences.l: And what is this filthy-one? Leave her away from you, and from your mind and your heart.
sentences.i: And what is this dirty creature to you? Leave her, and put her out of your mind and your heart.
sentences.n: أَيْشِ is the colloquial 'what?' (from أَيُّ شَيْءٍ 'which thing'), a Middle Arabic form that the reader will meet again. الْوَسِخَةُ is 'the filthy woman', the old woman's contemptuous word for the girl. Here she is pleading for the girl's life.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَكَتْ وَلَمْ تَزَلْ تُلِحُّ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى رَضِيَ وَقَالَ
sentences.tr: thumma bakat wa-lam tazal tulliḥḥu ʿalayhi ḥattā raḍiya wa-qāla
sentences.l: Then she wept, and did not cease pressing upon him until he was content, and said:
sentences.i: Then she wept, and kept pressing him until he relented, and said:

sentences.t: عَفَوْتُ عَنْهَا لَكِنْ لَابُدَّ أَنْ أَعْمَلَ أَثَرًا يَصِيرُ عَلَيْهَا بَقِيَّةَ عُمْرِهَا
sentences.tr: ʿafawtu ʿanhā lākin lābudda an aʿmala atharan yaṣīru ʿalayhā baqiyyata ʿumrihā
sentences.l: 'I have pardoned her; but it is unavoidable that I make a mark that becomes upon her for the remainder of her life.'
sentences.i: 'I pardon her; but I must leave a mark on her that will stay with her for the rest of her life.'
sentences.n: لَابُدَّ is printed as one word (Classical لَا بُدَّ), and is kept so.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرَ الْعَبِيدَ فَجَذَبُونِي وَمَدُّونِي بَعْدَ مَا جَرَّدُونِي مِنْ أَثْوَابِي
sentences.tr: thumma amara al-ʿabīda fa-jadhabūnī wa-maddūnī baʿda mā jarradūnī min athwābī
sentences.l: Then he ordered the slaves, and they pulled me and stretched me out after they had stripped me of my garments,
sentences.i: Then he ordered the slaves, and they dragged me and stretched me out, once they had stripped me of my clothes,

sentences.t: وَجَاسَتِ الْعَبِيدُ عَلَيَّ وَقَامَ الْغُلَامُ وَأَحْضَرَ قَضِيبًا مِنْ فَتَرَجَّلَ وَنَزَلَ بِهِ عَلَى جَسَدِي بِالضَّرْبِ
sentences.tr: wa-jāsati al-ʿabīdu ʿalayya wa-qāma al-ghulāmu wa-aḥḍara qaḍīban min fa-tarajjala wa-nazala bihi ʿalā jasadī bi-al-ḍarbi
sentences.l: And the slaves went about upon me, and the young man rose and brought a rod of, then he went-on-foot, and came down with it upon my body with beating,
sentences.i: The slaves held me down, and the young man got up and fetched a rod; then, on his feet, he brought it down on my body with blows,
sentences.n: Two spots are doubtful. وَجَاسَتِ 'went about, trod' is probably a slip for جَلَسَتِ 'sat' (the slaves sat on her to hold her down); it is read as printed and given the sense that suits the scene. قَضِيبًا مِنْ breaks off after مِنْ, as if the material of the rod (a cane, say) had dropped out; the next word فَتَرَجَّلَ 'then he dismounted, went on foot' is read as printed, and may hide a different word. Read them as rough spots, not as your mistake.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلْ يَضْرِبُنِي عَلَى ظَهْرِي وَأَجْنَابِي حَتَّى غِبْتُ عَنِ الْوُجُودِ مِنْ شِدَّةِ الضَّرْبِ وَقَدْ أَيِسْتُ مِنْ حَيَوٰتِي
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazal yaḍribunī ʿalā ẓahrī wa-ajnābī ḥattā ghibtu ʿani al-wujūdi min shiddati al-ḍarbi wa-qad ayistu min ḥayātī
sentences.l: And he did not cease striking me on my back and my sides until I was absent from existence from the violence of the beating, and I had despaired of my life.
sentences.i: And he never stopped beating my back and my sides until I lost all awareness of the world from the violence of the blows, and I had given up hope of my life.

sentences.t: فَأَمَرَ الْعَبِيدَ أَنَّهُ إِذَا دَخَلَ اللَّيْلُ يَحْمِلُونِي وَيَأْخُذُوا الْعَجُوزَ مَعَهُمْ تَدُلُّهُمْ عَلَى الْبَيْتِ وَيَرْمُونِي فِي بَيْتِي الَّذِي كُنْتُ فِيهِ سَابِقًا
sentences.tr: fa-amara al-ʿabīda annahu idhā dakhala al-laylu yaḥmilūnī wa-yaʾkhudhū al-ʿajūza maʿahum tadulluhum ʿalā al-bayti wa-yarmūnī fī baytī alladhī kuntu fīhi sābiqan
sentences.l: So he ordered the slaves that, when the night entered, they carry me and take the old woman with them, she guiding-them to the house, and throw me into my house in which I had been formerly.
sentences.i: Then he ordered the slaves that, when night fell, they should carry me off, taking the old woman with them to show them the house, and throw me into the house where I had lived before.
sentences.n: أَنَّهُ إِذَا ... يَحْمِلُونِي gives the order as a reported statement ('that, when night comes, they carry me') rather than with أَنْ and the subjunctive. The printed verbs يَحْمِلُونِي and يَرْمُونِي keep their plural ending, while وَيَأْخُذُوا drops it; all are read as printed. تَدُلُّهُمْ 'she guiding them' is a circumstantial clause.

sentences.t: فَفَعَلُوا مَا أَمَرَهُمْ بِهِ سَيِّدُهُمْ وَرَمَوْنِي فِي بَيْتِي وَرَاحُوا
sentences.tr: fa-faʿalū mā amarahum bihi sayyiduhum wa-ramawnī fī baytī wa-rāḥū
sentences.l: So they did what their master ordered them with, and threw me into my house, and went off.
sentences.i: They did as their master had commanded, threw me into my house, and went away.
sentences.n: أَمَرَ بِـ 'command (a thing)' takes بِـ for the thing commanded, so أَمَرَهُمْ بِهِ is 'he commanded them it'.

sentences.t: وَلَازَمْتُ أَنَا فِي غَشْوَتِي إِلَّا وَالصَّبَاحُ قَدْ لَاحَ
sentences.tr: wa-lāzamtu anā fī ghashwatī illā wa-al-ṣabāḥu qad lāḥa
sentences.l: And I kept-to, I, in my swoon, except that the morning had shone.
sentences.i: And I lay there in my swoon until the morning had dawned.
sentences.n: إِلَّا وَ... here means 'until, only when' ('I stayed in my swoon; it was only when the morning had dawned...'), a Middle Arabic use of إِلَّا with a following state clause. The sentence stops short of saying what happened at dawn; the next unit supplies it.

sentences.t: فَلَاطَفْتُ حَالِي فِى الْمَرَاهِمِ وَالْأَدْوِيَةِ وَدَاوَيْتُ جِسْمِي وَبَقِيَتْ أَضْلَاعِي كَأَنَّهَا مَضْرُوبَةٌ بِالْمَقَارِعِ كَمَا تَرَي
sentences.tr: fa-lāṭaftu ḥālī fī al-marāhimi wa-al-adwiyati wa-dāwaytu jismī wa-baqiyat aḍlāʿī ka-annahā maḍrūbatun bi-al-maqāriʿi kamā tarā
sentences.l: So I treated-gently my condition with the salves and the medicines, and I doctored my body, and my ribs remained as though they were beaten with the scourges, as you see.
sentences.i: So I nursed myself with salves and medicines and doctored my body, yet my ribs remain as though they had been flogged with rods, as you see.
sentences.n: She is showing the caliph her scars, hence كَمَا تَرَى 'as you see' (printed with ي). كَأَنَّهَا is كَـ + أَنَّ + هَا 'as though she/it'. الْمَقَارِعِ is the plural of مِقْرَعَة 'a whip or rod for beating'.

sentences.t: وَ رَقَدْتُ ضَعِيفَةً طَرِيحَةَ الْفِرَاشِ أُدَاوِي رُوحِي أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ حَتَّى اسْتَفَقْتُ وَ شُفِيتُ
sentences.tr: wa-raqadtu ḍaʿīfatan ṭarīḥata al-firāshi udāwī rūḥī arbaʿata ashhurin ḥattā istafaqtu wa-shufītu
sentences.l: And I lay down, weak, thrown-down of the bed, doctoring my spirit, four months, until I came-round and was healed,
sentences.i: And I lay four months, weak and bedridden, tending myself, until I came to my senses and was cured,
sentences.n: رُوحِي 'my spirit' stands for 'myself'.

sentences.t: وَجِئْتُ إِلَى الدَّارِ الَّتِي جَرَى لِي فِيهَا ذَٰلِكَ الْأَمْرُ فَوَجَدْتُهَا خَرَابًا وَالزُّقَاقَ مَهْدُودًا مِنْ أَوَّلِهِ إِلَى آخِرِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-jiʾtu ilā al-dāri allatī jarā lī fīhā dhālika al-amru fa-wajadtuhā kharāban wa-al-zuqāqa mahdūdan min awwalihi ilā ākhirihi
sentences.l: And I came to the house in which that matter had happened to me, and I found it a ruin, and the lane demolished from its first to its last,
sentences.i: I went to the house where that affair had befallen me, and found it in ruins, and the whole lane pulled down from one end to the other,
sentences.n: الزُّقَاقَ مَهْدُودًا is a second object of وَجَدْتُهَا: 'I found the house a ruin and the lane demolished'.

sentences.t: وَصَارَتِ الدَّارُ كِيمَانًا وَلَمْ أَعْلَمْ خَبَرَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-ṣārati al-dāru kīmānan wa-lam aʿlam khabarahā
sentences.l: and the house had become mounds, and I did not know its news.
sentences.i: and the house had become heaps of rubble, and I could learn nothing of what had become of it.
sentences.n: كِيمَانًا is the plural of كَوْم / كُوم 'heap, mound'; in the Egyptian idiom of the Nights, 'mounds of rubble'.

sentences.t: فَجِئْتُ إِلَى أُخْتِي هَٰذِهِ الَّتِي مِنْ أَبِي فَوَجَدْتُ عِنْدَهَا هَانَيْنِ الْكَلْبَتَيْنِ السُّودِ فَسَلَّمْتُ عَلَيْهَا وَأَخْبَرْتُهَا بِخَبَرِي وَجَمِيعِ حَدِيثِي
sentences.tr: fa-jiʾtu ilā ukhtī hādhihi allatī min abī fa-wajadtu ʿindahā hānayni al-kalbatayni al-sūdi fa-sallamtu ʿalayhā wa-akhbartuhā bi-khabarī wa-jamīʿi ḥadīthī
sentences.l: So I came to my sister, this one, who is from my father, and I found with her these two bitches, the black-ones, and I greeted her, and informed her of my news and all my tale,
sentences.i: Then I went to my sister here, the one by my father's side, and found with her these two black bitches. I greeted her and told her my news and the whole of my tale,
sentences.n: هَانَيْنِ is printed with ن where Classical Arabic has هَاتَيْنِ 'these two (f.)'; it is read as printed and is a slip or dialect form. السُّودِ is a plural adjective beside a dual noun, as in the opening of the story. أَخْبَرَ بِـ 'inform of' takes بِـ with what is told. أُخْتِي هَٰذِهِ الَّتِي مِنْ أَبِي is 'my sister, the one from my father', that is, a half-sister on the father's side.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لِي يَا أُخْتِي مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي مِنْ نَكَبَاتِ الزَّمَانِ سَلِمَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي جَاءَ الْأَمْرُ بِسَلَامَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lī yā ukhtī man dhā alladhī min nakabāti al-zamāni salima al-ḥamdu li-Allāhi alladhī jāʾa al-amru bi-salāmatin
sentences.l: So she said to me: 'O my sister, who is this one who, from the calamities of time, is safe? Praise be to God that the matter came with safety,'
sentences.i: She said to me, 'Sister, who is there that escapes the misfortunes of time? Praise God that the matter has come to a safe end,'
sentences.n: الَّذِي after الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ works as 'that' ('praise be to God that...'), as a conjunction rather than a relative: a Middle Arabic use. مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي is the rhetorical 'who is it that...?'.

sentences.t: وَجَعَلَتْ تَقُولُ
sentences.tr: wa-jaʿalat taqūlu
sentences.l: and she began saying:
sentences.i: and she began to recite:

sentences.t: وَمَا الدَّهْرُ إِلَّا هَكَذَا فَاصْطَبِرْ بِهِ * إِذَا رُزِيتَ بِمَالٍ أَوْ فِرَاقِ حَبِيبِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā al-dahru illā hākadhā fa-iṣṭabir bihi * idhā ruziyta bi-mālin aw firāqi ḥabībi
sentences.l: And time is nothing but thus, so be patient with it * when you are afflicted in property or in the parting of a beloved.
sentences.i: Such is Time, and nothing else; so bear it with patience when you are struck by loss of wealth or the parting of a friend.
sentences.n: The verse is unpointed in the archive, so the vowels are ours. رُزِيتَ is printed without the hamza that رُزِئْتَ 'you were afflicted' has; it is read as printed. رُزِئَ بِـ 'be afflicted with (a loss)' takes بِـ with the loss. The final -i of حَبِيبِ follows the rhyme.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَخْبَرَتْنِي بِخَبَرِهَا وَمَا جَرَى لَهَا مَعَ أَخَوَاتِهَا وَمَا قَدْ صَارُوا إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: thumma akhbaratnī bi-khabarihā wa-mā jarā lahā maʿa akhawātihā wa-mā qad ṣārū ilayhi
sentences.l: Then she informed me of her news and of what had happened to her with her sisters and of what they had come to.
sentences.i: Then she told me her own story, and what had passed between her and her sisters, and what had become of them.

sentences.t: فَقَعَدْتُ أَنَا وَهِيَ لَا نَذْكُرُ خَبَرَ الزَّوَاجِ عَلَى أَلْسِنَتِنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qaʿadtu anā wa-hiya lā nadhkuru khabara al-zawāji ʿalā alsinatinā
sentences.l: So I sat, I and she, not mentioning the news of marriage upon our tongues.
sentences.i: So she and I settled down together, never letting the word 'marriage' pass our lips.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ صَاحِبَتُنَا هَٰذِهِ الصَّبِيَّةُ الْخُوشْكَاشَةُ فِي كُلِّ يَوْمٍ تَخْرُجُ تَشْتَرِي لَنَا مَا نَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ مِنَ الْمَصَالِحِ فِي يَوْمِنَا وَلَيْلَتِنَا
sentences.tr: thumma ṣāḥibatunā hādhihi al-ṣabiyyatu al-khūshkāshatu fī kulli yawmin takhruju tashtarī lanā mā naḥtāju ilayhi mina al-maṣāliḥi fī yawminā wa-laylatinā
sentences.l: Then our companion, this girl, the khūshkāsha, in every day would go out, buying for us what we need of the needs of our day and our night.
sentences.i: Then our companion, this girl, our comrade, went out every day to buy what we needed for our day and night.
sentences.n: الْخُوشْكَاشَةُ is obscure. It may be the Persian-Turkish khōshdāsh 'comrade, fellow-servant' in a corrupt spelling; I render it 'comrade' and cannot be sure. The verb takhruju is a habitual present ('used to go out').

sentences.t: وَصِرْنَا عَلَى هَٰذِهِ الْحَالَةِ إِلَى هَٰذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ الَّتِي مَضَتْ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣirnā ʿalā hādhihi al-ḥālati ilā hādhihi al-laylati allatī maḍat
sentences.l: And we became upon this state until this night that has passed,
sentences.i: and so we went on until last night,

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَتْ أُخْتُنَا تَشْتَرِي لَنَا شَيْئًا عَلَى جَرْيِ عَادَتِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-kharajat ukhtunā tashtarī lanā shayʾan ʿalā jaryi ʿādatihā
sentences.l: and our sister went out, buying for us something, on the running of her custom,
sentences.i: and our sister went out, as was her habit, to buy something for us,

sentences.t: فَوَقَعَ لَنَا مَا وَقَعَ بِمَجِئِ الْحَمَّالِ وَهَؤُلَاءِ الثَّلَٰثَةِ الْقَرَنْدَلِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-waqaʿa lanā mā waqaʿa bi-majiʾi al-ḥammāli wa-hāʾulāʾi al-thalāthati al-qarandaliyyati
sentences.l: and there befell us what befell, with the coming of the porter and these three qalandars,
sentences.i: and then there befell us what you know, with the coming of the porter and these three dervishes,
sentences.n: الْقَرَنْدَلِيَّةِ is 'the qalandars' (Persian qalandar, a wandering dervish), spelled here with ر. The dagger alif over ثَلَٰثَةِ supplies the alif the edition leaves out of ثلثة.

sentences.t: فَتَحَادَثْنَا مَعَهُمْ وَأَدْخَلْنَاهُمْ عِنْدَنَا وَأَكْرَمْنَاهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-taḥādathnā maʿahum wa-adkhalnāhum ʿindanā wa-akramnāhum
sentences.l: and we conversed with them, and brought them in to us, and honoured them,
sentences.i: We talked with them, took them in, and made them welcome,

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَذْهَبْ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ بُرْهَةٌ حَتَّى اجْتَمَعْنَا بِثَلَٰثَةِ تُجَّارٍ مُحْتَشِمِينَ مِنَ الْمَوْصِلِ وَحَكَوْنَا حَدِيثَهُمْ وَتَحَادَثْنَا مَعَهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yadhhab mina al-layli burhatun ḥattā ijtamaʿnā bi-thalāthati tujjārin muḥtashimīna mina al-Mawṣili wa-ḥakawnā ḥadīthahum wa-taḥādathnā maʿahum
sentences.l: and there had not gone from the night a while until we met with three merchants, dignified-ones, from Mosul, and they related to-us their tale, and we conversed with them,
sentences.i: Hardly a moment of the night had gone before we fell in with three respectable merchants from Mosul; they told us their story, and we talked with them,
sentences.n: وَحَكَوْنَا حَدِيثَهُمْ has -nā 'us' attached directly to the verb as an object, where Classical Arabic would say حَكَوْا لَنَا 'they related to us'; a Middle Arabic feature. اجْتَمَعَ بِـ 'meet with, fall in with' takes بِـ with the person met.

sentences.t: وَكُنَّا شَرَطْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ شَرْطًا فَخَالَفُونَا فِيهِ
sentences.tr: wa-kunnā sharaṭnā ʿalayhim sharṭan fa-khālafūnā fīhi
sentences.l: and we had stipulated upon them a condition, and they contravened us in it,
sentences.i: We had laid one condition upon them, and they broke it,

sentences.t: فَإِنَّنَا قَابَلْنَاهُمْ عَلَى مُخَالَفَتِهِمْ وَاسْتَخْبَرْنَاهُمْ عَمَّا جَرَى لَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-innanā qābalnāhum ʿalā mukhālafatihim wa-istakhbarnāhum ʿammā jarā lahum
sentences.l: for we requited them upon their contravention, and asked-them-the-news of what had happened to them,
sentences.i: and we repaid them for their breach, and questioned them about what had happened to them,

sentences.t: فَحَكَوْا لَنَا حِكَايَتَهُمْ وَمَا جَرَى لَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥakaw lanā ḥikāyatahum wa-mā jarā lahum
sentences.l: so they related to us their story and what had happened to them,
sentences.i: and they told us their tale and all that had befallen them,

sentences.t: فَعَفَوْنَا عَنْهُمْ وَانْفَصَلُوا عَنَّا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿafawnā ʿanhum wa-infaṣalū ʿannā
sentences.l: so we pardoned them, and they parted from us,
sentences.i: and we forgave them, and they took their leave of us,

sentences.t: وَمَا نَشْعُرُ الْيَوْمَ حَتَّى حَضَرْنَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ وَهَٰذِةْ حِكَايَتُنَا
sentences.tr: wa-mā nashʿuru al-yawma ḥattā ḥaḍarnā bayna yadayka wa-hādhihi ḥikāyatunā
sentences.l: and we did not perceive, today, until we were present between your two hands; and this is our story.
sentences.i: and before we knew it today, we stood in your presence. That is our story.
sentences.n: هَٰذِةْ is the edition's spelling with ة for هَٰذِهِ 'this (f.)'; it is read as printed, with the ending dropped as at a pause. بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ 'between your two hands' is the stock phrase for 'in your presence'.

sentences.t: فَتَعَجَّبَ الْخَلِيفَةُ مِنْهَا وَجَعَلَ لَهَا تَارِيخًا فِي خِزَانَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-taʿajjaba al-khalīfatu minhā wa-jaʿala lahā tārīkhan fī khizānatihi
sentences.l: So the caliph marvelled at it, and made for it a dated-record in his treasury.
sentences.i: The caliph marvelled at the story and had it set down in the records of his treasury.
sentences.n: خِزَانَة may be 'treasury' or 'library, archive'; تَارِيخ here is a dated record or chronicle.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazad, so she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Then morning overtook Shahrazad, and she broke off her tale.
sentences.n: This is the stock formula that closes each night, in rhymed prose (sajʿ): الصَّبَاحُ and الْمُبَاحِ share the rhyme -āḥ. الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ is 'the permitted speech', the tale she is free to tell.
